name: methylidyne
label: mol:CH
note: *First radio in Rydbeck et al. 1973 Nature 246, 466
latex_body: \citet{Swings:1937:483} suggested that an observed line at $\lambda = 4300$~\AA~by \citet{Dunham:1937:26} using the Mount Wilson Observatory in diffuse gas toward a number of supergiant B stars might have been due to the $^2\Delta \leftarrow ^2\Pi$ transition of CH, reported in the laboratory by \citet{Jevons:1932:177}.  \citet{McKellar:1940:187} later identified several additional transitions in observational data.  The first radio identification was reported by \citet{Rydbeck:1973:466} at 3335~MHz with the Onsala telescope toward more than a dozen sources using estimated fundamental rotational transition frequencies from \citet{Shklovsky:1953:25}, \citet{Goss:1966:707}, and \citet{Baird:1971:L83}.  The first direct measurement of the CH rotational spectrum was reported by \citet{Brazier:1983:1608}.

name: cyano radical
label: mol:CN
note: *First radio in Jefferts et al. 1970 ApJ 161, L87
latex_body: Lines of CN were first reported using the Mount Wilson Observatory around $\lambda = 3875$~\AA~by \citet{McKellar:1940:187} and \citet{Adams:1941:11} based on the laboratory work of \citet{Jenkins:1938:137}. Later, \citet{Jefferts:1970:L87} reported the first detection of rotational emission from CN by observation of the $J = 1-0$ transition at 113.5~GHz in Orion and W51 using the NRAO 36-ft telescope.  Identification was made prior to laboratory observation of the rotational transitions of CN, and was based on rotational constants derived from electronic transitions measured by \citet{Poletto:1965:519} and dipole moments measured by \citet{Thomson:1968:2815}.  The laboratory rotational spectra were first measured seven years later by \citet{Dixon:1977:3956}.

name: methylidyne cation
label: mol:CH+
latex_body: \citet{Swings:1937:483} suggested that a set of three lines at $\lambda =$~4233, 3958, and 3745~\AA~seen with the Mount Wilson Observatory in diffuse gas belonged to a diatomic cation.  \citet{Douglas:1941:381} confirmed the assignment to \ce{CH^+} by laboratory observation of these lines in the $^1\Pi \leftarrow ^1\Sigma$ transition.  The first observation of rotational transitions of \ce{CH^+} was reported by \citet{Cernicharo:1997:L65} toward NGC 7027 using ISO, and based on rotational constants derived from rovibronic transitions measured by \citet{Carrington:1982:272}.

name: hydroxyl radical
label: mol:OH
latex_body: \citet{Weinreb:1963:829} reported the first detection of OH through observation of its ground state, $^2\Pi _{3/2}$, $J = 3/2$, $\Lambda$-doubled, $F = 2\rightarrow2$ and $F = 1\rightarrow1$ hyperfine transitions at 1666~MHz toward Cas A using the Millstone Hill Observatory.  The frequencies were measured in the laboratory by \citet{Ehrenstein:1959:40}.

name: carbon monoxide
label: mol:CO
latex_body: \citet{Wilson:1970:L43} reported the observation of the $J = 1\rightarrow0$ transition of CO toward Orion using the NRAO 36-ft telescope at a (velocity-shifted) frequency of 115267.2~MHz, based on a rest frequency of 115271.2~MHz from \citet{Cord:1968:}.

name: hydrogen
label: mol:H2
latex_body: Molecular hydrogen was reported by \citet{Carruthers:1970:L81} toward $\xi$~Per using a spectrograph on an Aerobee-150 rocket launched from White Sands Missile Range.  The $B^1\Sigma _u \leftarrow X^1\Sigma _g$ Lyman series in the range of 1000--1400~\AA~was observed and identified by direct comparison to a absorption cell observed with the same instrument used for the rocket observations.

name: silicon monoxide
label: mol:SiO
latex_body: The $J=3\rightarrow2$ transition of SiO at 130246~MHz was observed by \citet{Wilson:1971:L97} toward Sgr~B2 using the NRAO 36-ft telescope.  The transition frequency was calculated based on the laboratory work of \citet{Raymonda:1970:3458} and \citet{Torring:1968:777}.  SiO was the first confirmed silicon-containing species in the ISM.

name: carbon monosulfide
label: mol:CS
latex_body: \citet{Penzias:1971:L53} reported the detection of the $J = 3\rightarrow2$ transition of CS at 146969~MHz toward Orion, W51, IRC+10216, and DR21 using the NRAO 36-ft telescope.  The laboratory microwave spectrum was first reported by \citet{Mockler:1955:1837}. CS was the first confirmed sulfur-containing species in the ISM.

name: sulfur monoxide
label: mol:SO
latex_body: An unidentified line in NRAO 36-ft observations of Orion was assigned to the $J_K = 3_2\rightarrow2_1$ transition of SO by \citet{Gottlieb:1973:L59} based on laboratory data from \citet{Winnewisser:1964:1687}.  The authors subsequently observed SO emission toward numerous other sources, as well as identifying the $4_3\rightarrow3_2$ transition using the 16-ft telescope at McDonald Observatory.  SO was the first molecule detected in space in a $^3\Sigma$ ground electronic state via radio astronomy.

name: silicon monosulfide
label: mol:SiS
latex_body: \citet{Morris:1975:L47} reported the detection of the $J = 6\rightarrow5$ and $5\rightarrow4$ transitions of SiS at 108924.6~MHz and 90771.85~MHz, respectively, based on the laboratory work of \citet{Hoeft:1965:1327}.  The observations were conducted toward IRC+10216 using the NRAO 36-ft telescope.

name: nitrogen monosulfide
label: mol:NS
latex_body: \citet{Gottlieb:1975:L147} and \citet{Kuiper:1975:L151} simultaneously and independently reported the detection of NS.  \citet{Gottlieb:1975:L147} observed the $J=5/2\rightarrow3/2$ transition in the $^2\Pi_{1/2}$ electronic state at 115154~MHz \citep{Amano:1969:97} toward Sgr B2 using the 16-ft antenna at the University of Texas Millimeter Wave Observatory over three periods in 1973--1974, and confirmed the detection using the NRAO 36-ft telescope in May 1975.  \citet{Kuiper:1975:L151} observed the same transitions toward Sgr B2 using the NRAO 36-ft telescope in February 1975.

name: dicarbon
label: mol:C2
latex_body: The detection of \ce{C2} was reported by \citet{Souza:1977:L49} toward Cygnus OB2 No. 12 using the Smithsonian Institution's Mount Hopkins Observatory.  The detected lines at 10140~\AA~were measured in the laboratory by \citet{Phillips:1948:389}.

name: nitric oxide
label: mol:NO
latex_body: \citet{Liszt:1978:L73} reported the identification of NO in the ISM toward Sgr B2 using the NRAO 36-ft telescope.  The detection was based on the laboratory analysis of the hyperfine-splitting in the $^2\Pi_{1/2}$ $J = 3/2\rightarrow1/2$ transition near 150.1~GHz as reported in \citet{Gallagher:1956:1727}.

name: hydrogen chloride
label: mol:HCl
latex_body: Interstellar H$^{35}$Cl was reported by \citet{Blake:1985:501} who used the Kuiper Airborne Observatory to observe the $J = 1\rightarrow0$ transition at 625918.8~MHz toward Orion.  The laboratory transition frequencies were reported in \citet{deLucia:1971:1849}.

name: sodium chloride
label: mol:NaCl
latex_body: The detection of NaCl was reported by \citet{Cernicharo:1987:L10} toward IRC+10216 using IRAM 30-m observations of six transitions between 91--169~GHz, as well as the $J=8\rightarrow7$ transition of \ce{Na^{37}Cl} at 101961.9~MHz.  The laboratory frequencies were obtained from \citet{Lovas:1974:609}.

name: aluminum chloride
label: mol:AlCl
latex_body: The detection of AlCl was reported by \citet{Cernicharo:1987:L10} toward IRC+10216 using IRAM 30-m observations of four transitions between 87--160~GHz, as well as the $J=10\rightarrow9$ and $11\rightarrow10$ transitions of \ce{Al^{37}Cl} at 142322.5~MHz and 156546.8~MHz, respectively.  The laboratory frequencies were obtained from \citet{Lovas:1974:609}.

events.summary: Replaced placeholder dipole moment with the computed AlCl mu_a value from Yousefi:2018:8.

name: potassium chloride
label: mol:KCl
latex_body: The detection of KCl was reported by \citet{Cernicharo:1987:L10} toward IRC+10216 using IRAM 30-m observations of six transitions between 100--161~GHz.  The laboratory frequencies were obtained from \citet{Lovas:1974:609}.

name: aluminum fluoride
label: mol:AlF
note: *Confirmed in 1994 ApJ 433, 729
latex_body: \citet{Cernicharo:1987:L10} claimed a tentative detection of AlF toward IRC+10216 using IRAM 30-m observations of three transitions between 99--165~GHz.  The laboratory frequencies were obtained from \citet{Lovas:1974:609}. The detection was confirmed by \citet{Ziurys:1994:729} using CSO observations of IRC+10216.  Three additional lines, the $J=7\rightarrow6$, $8\rightarrow7$, and $10\rightarrow9$ were observed at 230793, 263749, and 329642~MHz, respectively, based on laboratory data from \citet{Wyse:1970:3887}.

name: phosphorous mononitride
label: mol:PN
note: *Confirmed in Turner & Bally 1987 ApJ 321, L75 and Ziurys 1987 ApJ 321 L81
latex_body: \citet{Sutton:1985:341} first suggested that a feature observed in their line survey data using the OVRO 10.4-m telescope toward Orion at 234936~MHz could be attributed to the $J = 5\rightarrow4$ transition of PN, using the laboratory data reported in \citet{Wyse:1972:1106}.  \citet{Turner:1987:L75} and \citet{Ziurys:1987:L81} later simultaneously confirmed the detection of PN.  \citet{Turner:1987:L75} observed the $2\rightarrow1$, $3\rightarrow2$, and $5\rightarrow4$ transitions at 93980, 140968, and 234936~MHz, respectively, toward Orion, W51, and Sgr B2 using the NRAO 12-m telescope. \citet{Ziurys:1987:L81} observed the  $2\rightarrow1$, $3\rightarrow2$, and $5\rightarrow4$ transitions toward Orion using the FCRAO 14-m telescope, and the $6\rightarrow5$ using the NRAO 12-m telescope.  The $2\rightarrow1$ transition was also observed toward Sgr B2 and W51.  PN was the first phosphorous-containing molecule detected in the ISM.

name: silicon carbide
label: mol:SiC
latex_body: \citet{Cernicharo:1989:L25} reported the detection of the SiC radical in IRC+10216 using the IRAM 30-m telescope.  Fine structure and $\Lambda$-doubled lines were detected in the $J = 2\rightarrow1$, $4\rightarrow3$, and $6\rightarrow5$ transitions in the $^3\Pi$ electronic ground state near 81, 162, and 236~GHz, respectively, based on laboratory data presented in the same manuscript.  The authors make note of unidentified lines suggestive of the SiC radical in earlier data toward IRC+10216 beginning in 1976, both in their own observations and in those of I. Dubois (unpublished) using the NRAO 36-ft telescope.

name: carbon monophosphide
label: mol:CP

dipole.note: Computed as part of this work; calculation notebook: docs/calculations/cp_dipole_calculations.ipynb.

latex_body: \citet{Saito:1989:1114} measured the rotational spectrum of CP in the laboratory and conducted an astronomical search for the $N = 1\rightarrow0$ and $2\rightarrow1$ transitions at 48 and 96~GHz, respectively, using the Nobeyama 45-m telescope across several sources, resulting in non-detections.  \citet{Guelin:1990:L9} subsequently reported the successful detection of the $2\rightarrow1$ and $5\rightarrow4$ (239~GHz) transitions toward IRC+10216 using the IRAM 30-m telescope.  The dipole moment was calculated as part of this work (\ref{sec:dipole}).

events.summary: Replaced placeholder dipole moment with this-work computed CP mu_a value and documented the calculation provenance with a manuscript cross-reference.

name: imidogen radical
label: mol:NH
note: *First radio in Cernicharo et al. 2000 ApJ 534, L199
latex_body: \citet{Meyer:1991:L49} reported the detection of the $A^3\Pi-X^3\Sigma$ (0,0) $R_1$(0) line of NH in absorption toward $\xi$ Per and HD 27778 at 3358~\AA~using the KPNO 4-m telescope.  The laboratory rest frequencies were obtained from \citet{Dixon:1959:1171}.  The earliest reported detection of rotational transitions of NH appears to be that of \citet{Cernicharo:2000:L199}, who observed the $N_J = 2_3\rightarrow1_2$ transition at 974~GHz toward Sgr B2 with ISO.  Although no laboratory reference is given, the frequencies used were presumably those of \citet{Klaus:1997:L1}.

name: silicon nitride
label: mol:SiN
latex_body: \citet{Turner:1992:L35} reported the detection of the $N=2\rightarrow1$ and $6\rightarrow5$ transitions of SiN at 87 and 262~GHz, respectively, toward IRC+10216 using the NRAO 12-m telescope.  The $2\rightarrow1$ transition was measured by \citet{Saito:1983:6447}, and the frequency for the $6\rightarrow5$ was calculated from the constants given therein.

name: sulfur monoxide cation
label: mol:SO+

dipole.note: Computed as part of this work; calculation notebook: docs/calculations/sop_dipole_calculations.ipynb.

latex_body: The detection of \ce{SO^+} was reported by \citet{Turner:1992:L107} toward IC 443G using the NRAO 12-m telescope.  The $\Lambda$-doubled $^2\Pi_{1/2}$, $J = 5/2\rightarrow3/2$ and $9/2\rightarrow7/2$ transitions at 116 and 209~GHz, respectively, were observed.  The frequencies of the $5/2\rightarrow3/2$ transitions were measured by \citet{Amano:1991:519}, while those of the $9/2\rightarrow7/2$ transitions were calculated from the constants given therein.  The dipole moment was calculated as part of this work (\ref{sec:dipole}).

events.summary: Replaced placeholder dipole moment with this-work computed SO+ mu_a value and documented the calculation provenance with a manuscript cross-reference.

name: carbon monoxide cation
label: mol:CO+
latex_body: \ce{CO^+} was first observed toward M17SW and NGC 7027 using the NRAO 12-m telescope by \citet{Latter:1993:L97}. The $N=2\rightarrow1$, $J = 3/2\rightarrow1/2$ and $5/2\rightarrow3/2$ near 236~GHz and the $3\rightarrow2$, $5/2\rightarrow3/2$ were observed based on the laboratory work of \citet{Sastry:1981:L91}. An earlier reported detection of the $2\rightarrow1$, $5/2\rightarrow3/2$ transition in Orion by \citet{Erickson:1981:L83}, based on the laboratory data of \citet{Dixon:1975:61}, was later definitely assigned to transitions of \ce{^{13}CH3OH} by \citet{Blake:1984:586}.

name: hydrogen fluoride
label: mol:HF
latex_body: \citet{Neufeld:1997:L141} reported the detection of the $J = 2\rightarrow1$ transition of HF at 2.5~THz toward Sgr B2 using ISO.  The rest frequencies were measured in the laboratory by \citet{Nolt:1987:274}.

name: nitrogen
label: mol:N2
latex_body: \citet{Knauth:2004:636} observed the c$^{\prime}_4$$^1$$\Sigma_u^+$--$X^1$$\Sigma_g^+$ and c$_3$$^1$$\Sigma_u^+$--$X^1$$\Sigma_g^+$ transitions of \ce{N2} at 958.6 and 960.3~\AA~, respectively, using FUSE observations toward HD 124314.  The oscillator strengths of the c$^{\prime}_4$$^1 $$\Sigma_u^+$--$X^1\Sigma_g^+$ transition were obtained from \citet{Stark:2000:321}, and the c$_3$~$^1$$ \Sigma_u^+$--$X^1$$\Sigma_g^+$ transition from a private communication with G. Stark.

name: fluoromethylidynium cation
label: mol:CF+
latex_body: The detection of \ce{CF^+} was reported by \citet{Neufeld:2006:L37} using IRAM 30-m and APEX 12-m observations of the $J = 1\rightarrow0$, $2\rightarrow1$, and $3\rightarrow2$ transitions at 102.6, 205.2, and 307.7~GHz, respectively, toward the Orion Bar.  The laboratory frequencies were reported by \citet{Plummer:1986:2427}.

name: phosphorous monoxide
label: mol:PO
latex_body: \citet{Tenenbaum:2007:L29} reported the detection of the $\Lambda$-doubled $J = 11/2\rightarrow9/2$ and $13/2\rightarrow11/2$ transitions of PO at 240 and 284~GHz, respectively, using SMT 10-m observations of VY Canis Majoris.  Although not cited, the frequencies were presumably obtained from the laboratory work of \citet{Kawaguchi:1983:629} and \citet{Bailleux:2002:465}.

name: oxygen
label: mol:O2
note: *Also Larsson et al. 2007 A&A 466, 999; Tentative in Goldsmith 2002 ApJ 576, 814
latex_body: A tentative detection of molecular oxygen was reported by \citet{Goldsmith:2002:814} in SWAS observations of $\rho$ Oph, although more sensitive observations of the region by \citet{Pagani:2003:L77} using the Odin satellite could not confirm the detection, and set an upper limit 3 times lower than that of \citet{Goldsmith:2002:814}.  \ce{O2} was only definitely detected several years later by \citet{Larsson:2007:999} using observations of the $N_J = 1_1\rightarrow1_0$ transition at 118750 MHz, again with the Odin satellite toward $\rho$ Oph A.  Although no citation is provided, the frequencies were presumably obtained from the laboratory work of \citet{Endo:1982:L379}.  Later, \citet{Goldsmith:2011:96} reported the observation of the $N_J = 3_3\rightarrow1_2$, $5_4\rightarrow3_4$, and $7_6\rightarrow5_6$ transitions at 487, 774, and 1121~GHz, respectively, using \emph{Herschel}/HIFI observations of Orion.  Although there appears to be no citation to the laboratory data, these transition frequencies were likely taken from \citet{Drouin:2010:1167}.

name: aluminum monoxide
label: mol:AlO
latex_body: \citet{Tenenbaum:2009:L59} reported the detection of the $N = 7\rightarrow6$, $6\rightarrow5$, and $4\rightarrow3$ transitions of AlO at 268, 230, and 153~GHz, respectively, toward VY Canis Majoris using the SMT 10-m telescope.  The laboratory frequencies were reported in \citet{Yamada:1990:2146}.

name: cyanide anion
label: mol:CN-
latex_body: The detection of \ce{CN^-} was reported by \citet{Agundez:2010:L2} in observations of IRC+10216 using the IRAM 30-m telescope.  The $J = 1\rightarrow0$, $2\rightarrow1$, and $3\rightarrow2$ lines at 112.3, 224.5, and 336.8~GHz were observed, based on the laboratory work of \citet{Amano:2008:244305}.

name: hydroxyl cation
label: mol:OH+
latex_body: \ce{OH^+} was detected by \citet{Wyrowski:2010:A26} using APEX 12-m observations of Sgr B2.  The $N = 1\rightarrow0$, $J = 0\rightarrow1$ transitions were detected in absorption at 909~GHz based on the laboratory work of \citet{Bekooy:1985:3868}.  Nearly simultaneously, \citet{Benz:2010:L35} reported the detection of the $1\rightarrow0$, $3/2\rightarrow1/2$ transitions at 1033~GHz toward W3 IRS5 using \emph{Herschel}/HIFI, and \citet{Gerin:2010:L110} reported a detection along the line of sight to W31C, also with \emph{Herschel}/HIFI.

name: sulfanylium cation
label: mol:SH+
note: *Also in Menten et al. 2011 A&A 525, A77
latex_body: \citet{Benz:2010:L35} reported the detection of the $N_J = 1_2\rightarrow0_1$ transition of \ce{SH^+} at 526~GHz using \emph{Herschel}/HIFI observations of W3. Although only a reference to the CDMS database is given, the frequency was almost certainly based on the laboratory work of \citet{Hovde:1987:4332} and \citet{Brown:2009:68}. Although published after \citet{Benz:2010:L35}, the first \emph{submitted} detection appears to be that of \citet{Menten:2011:A77} who reported the detection of \ce{SH^+} in absorption toward Sgr B2, using the APEX 12-m telescope.  The $N_J = 1_1\rightarrow0_1$ transition at 683~GHz was observed based on the laboratory work of \citet{Hovde:1987:4332} and \citet{Brown:2009:68}. \citet{Benz:2010:L35} acknowledge the earlier submission of \citet{Menten:2011:A77} in their work.

name: hydrogen chloride cation
label: mol:HCl+
latex_body: The detection of \ce{HCl^+} was reported by \citet{DeLuca:2012:L37} in \emph{Herschel}/HIFI observations of W31C and W49N.  Hyperfine and $\Lambda$-doubling structure was observed in the $^2\Pi_{3/2}$ $J = 5/2\rightarrow3/2$ transition of \ce{H^{35}Cl^+} at 1.444 THz toward both sources, and the same transition of \ce{H^{37}Cl^+} was also observed toward W31C.  The laboratory work was described in \citet{Gupta:2012:L38}.

name: mercapto radical
label: mol:SH
latex_body: \citet{Neufeld:2012:L6} reported the detection of the $^2\Pi_{3/2}$ $J = 5/2\rightarrow3/2$ $\Lambda$-doubled transition of SH at 1383~GHz along the line of sight to W49A using the GREAT instrument on SOFIA.  The transition frequencies relied upon the work of \citet{Morino:1995:172} and \citet{Klisch:1996:1118}.

name: titanium monoxide
label: mol:TiO
latex_body: TiO was detected in VY Canis Majoris by \citet{Kaminski:2013:A113} using a combination of SMA and PdBI observations.  Several fine structure components in the $J = 11\rightarrow10$, $J = 10\rightarrow9$, $J = 9\rightarrow8$, and $J = 7\rightarrow6$ transitions were observed between 221 and 352~GHz based on the laboratory work of \citet{Namiki:1998:176}.

name: argonium
label: mol:ArH+
latex_body: Although a feature was initially observed in several \emph{Herschel} datasets near 618~GHz \citep{Neill:2014:8}, the attribution to \ce{^{36}ArH^+} was not readily apparent.  On Earth, \ce{^{40}Ar} is 300 times more abundant than  \ce{^{36}Ar} \citep{Lee:2006:4507}, and as no signal from \ce{^{40}ArH^+} was visible, \ce{^{36}ArH^+} seemed an unlikely carrier.  \citet{Barlow:2013:1343}, however, recognized that \ce{^{36}Ar} is the dominant isotope in the ISM \citep{Cameron:1973:121}, and identified the $J = 1\rightarrow0$ and $2\rightarrow1$ rotational lines of \ce{^{36}ArH^+} at 617.5 and 1234.6~GHz, respectively, in \emph{Herschel}/SPIRE spectra of the Crab Nebula.  A citation is only given to the CDMS database, as no laboratory data appears to exist for \ce{^{36}ArH^+}.  Instead, it is derived in the database to observational accuracy using isotopic scaling factors from other isotopologues.

name: nitrogen sulfide cation
label: mol:NS+
latex_body: \citet{Cernicharo:2018:L22} reported both the laboratory spectroscopy and astronomical identification of \ce{NS^+}.  The $J = 2\rightarrow1$ line has been observed with the IRAM 30-m telescope toward numerous sightlines, with confirming observations of the $3\rightarrow2$ and $5\rightarrow4$ in several.

name: helium hydride cation
label: mol:HeH+
note: Dipole moment from Engel et al. 2005 MNRAS 357, 471 using equilibrium internuclear separation value of 1.45 from Peyerimhoff 1965 JCP 43, 998
latex_body: \citet{Gusten:2019:357} reported both the astronomical identification of \ce{HeH^+} in SOFIA observations of NGC 7027.  The $J = 1\rightarrow0$ line was observed to have the same velocity profile as the CO $J = 11\rightarrow10$ in the same source.  The identification was made based on the laboratory work of \citet{Perry:2014:101101}.

name: vanadium oxide
label: mol:VO
note: Some VO transitions originally observed in the source by Wallerstein & Gonzalez 2001 PASP 113, 954, Wallerstein 1971 ApJ 169, 195, and Wallerstein 1986 ApJ 164, 101, but not assigned as circumstellar until now.  B constant from Cheung et al. 1982 JMS 91, 165.  Dipole moment from Suenram et al. 1991 JMS 148, 114.

name: silicon phosphide
label: mol:SiP
note: Dipole moment from Ornellas et al. 2000 ApJ 538, 675

name: iron carbide
label: mol:FeC
note: Dipole moment from Steimle et al. 2002 JCP 117, 1511

name: magnesium sulfide
label: mol:MgS
note: Dipole moment from Chambaud et al. 2008 Chem. Phys. 352, 147

name: sodium sulfide
label: mol:NaS
note: Dipole moment from Chambaud et al. 2008 Chem. Phys. 352, 147

name: water
label: mol:H2O
latex_body: \citet{Cheung:1969:626} reported the detection of the $J_{K_a,K_c} = 6_{1,6}\rightarrow5_{2,3}$ transition of \ce{H2O} at 22.2~GHz using the Hat Creek Observatory toward Sgr B2, Orion, and W49.  No citation to the laboratory data appears to be given, but presumably was obtained from the work of \citet{Golden:1948:92}.

name: formylium cation
label: mol:HCO+
latex_body: \citet{Buhl:1970:267} first reported the discovery of a bright emission feature at 89190~MHz toward Orion, W51, W3(OH), L134, and Sgr A in observations with the NRAO 36-ft telescope, and named the carrier `X-ogen.'  Shortly thereafter, \citet{Klemperer:1970:1230} suggested the attribution of this line to \ce{HCO^+}.  The detection and attribution was confirmed by the laboratory observation of \ce{HCO^+} by \citet{Woods:1975:1269}.

name: hydrogen cyanide
label: mol:HCN
latex_body: The first reported detection of HCN was that of \citet{Snyder:1971:L47} who observed the ground state $J = 1\rightarrow0$ transition at 88.6~GHz toward W3(OH), Orion, Sgr A, W49, W51, and DR 21 using the NRAO 36-ft telescope.  The enabling laboratory spectroscopy was reported by \citet{Delucia:1969:58}.

name: carbonyl sulfide
label: mol:OCS
latex_body: Emission from the $J = 9\rightarrow8$ transition of OCS at 109463~MHz toward Sgr B2 was reported by \citet{Jefferts:1971:L111} using the NRAO 36-ft telescope.  The laboratory spectroscopy was reported in \citet{King:1954:407}.

name: hydrogen isocyanide
label: mol:HNC
latex_body: Both \citet{Zuckerman:1972:L125} and \citet{Snyder:1972:17} observed unidentified emission signal at 90.7~GHz using the NRAO 36-ft telescope toward W51 and NGC 2264, respectively.  \citet{Snyder:1972:17} suggested this line to be due to HNC, which was confirmed four years later with the first laboratory measurement of the $J = 1\rightarrow0$ transition in the laboratory by \citet{Blackman:1976:395}.

name: hydrogen sulfide
label: mol:H2S
latex_body: \citet{Thaddeus:1972:L73} reported the detection of the $J_{K_a,K_c} = 1_{1,0}\rightarrow1_{0,1}$ transition of \emph{ortho}-\ce{H2S} at 168.7~GHz toward a number of sources with the NRAO 36-ft telescope.  The laboratory transition frequencies were measured by \citet{Cupp:1968:60}.

name: protonated nitrogen
label: mol:N2H+
latex_body: \citet{Turner:1974:L83} first reported an unidentified emission line at 93.174~GHz in NRAO 36-ft telescope toward a number of sources, including Sgr B2, DR 21(OH), NGC 2264, and NGC 6334N.  In a companion letter, \citet{Green:1974:L89} suggested the carrier was \ce{N2H^+}, based on theoretical calculations.  \citet{Thaddeus:1975:L25} claim the following year to have confirmed the detection by observing an exceptional match to the predicted \ce{^{14}N} hyperfine splitting.  Laboratory work by \citet{Saykally:1976:L101} solidified the detection.

name: ethynyl radical
label: mol:C2H
latex_body: The detection of \ce{C2H} was reported by \citet{Tucker:1974:L115} through observation of four $\lambda$-doubled, hyperfine components of the $N = 1\rightarrow0$ transition near 87.3~GHz in NRAO 36-ft telescope observations of Orion and numerous other sources.  The assignment was made based on a calculated rotational constant under the assumption that the \ce{C\bond{1}H} and \ce{C\bond{3}C} bonds had the same length as those already known in acetylene (\ce{C2H2}).  A linear structure was assumed based on the laboratory work of \citet{Cochran:1964:213} and \citet{Graham:1974:3817}.  The confirming laboratory microwave spectroscopy was later reported by \citet{Sastry:1981:L119}.

name: sulfur dioxide
label: mol:SO2
latex_body: \ce{SO2} was reported in NRAO 36-ft telescope observations toward Orion and Sgr B2 by \citet{Snyder:1975:L81}.  The $J_{K_a,K_c} = 8_{1,7}\rightarrow8_{0,8}$, $8_{3,5}\rightarrow9_{2,8}$, and $7_{3,5}\rightarrow8_{2,6}$ transitions at 83.7, 86.6, and 97.7~GHz, respectively, were observed in emission.  The enabling laboratory microwave spectroscopy work was performed by \citet{Steenbeckeliers:1968:331} with additional computation analysis performed by \citet{Kirchhoff:1972:333}.

name: formyl radical
label: mol:HCO
latex_body: \citet{Snyder:1976:L91} reported the detection of the $N_{K_-,K_+} = 1_{0,1} - 0_{0,0}$, $J = 3/2\rightarrow1/2$, $F = 2\rightarrow1$ transition of HCO at 86671~MHz toward W3, NGC 2024, W51, and K3-50 using the NRAO 36-ft telescope.  The laboratory microwave spectroscopy was reported by \citet{Saito:1972:L95}.

name: nitroxyl radical
label: mol:HNO
latex_body: The detection of HNO was first reported by \citet{Ulich:1977:L105} who observed the $J_{K_a,K_c} = 1_{0,1}\rightarrow0_{0,0}$ transition at 81477~MHz toward Sgr B2 and NGC 2024 using the NRAO 36-ft telescope.  The laboratory frequency was measured by \citet{Saito:1973:99}.  The initial detection was subject to significant controversy in the literature (see \citealt{Snyder:1993:L17}).  Subsequent observation of additional lines by \citet{Hollis:1991:407} and \citet{Ziurys:1994:706} confirmed the initial detection, aided by the laboratory work of \citet{Sastry:1984:563}.

name: protonated carbon monosulfide
label: mol:HCS+
latex_body: \citet{Thaddeus:1981:L41} reported the detection of four harmonically spaced, unidentified lines in NRAO 36-ft and Bell 7-m telescope observations of Orion and Sgr B2.  Based on the harmonic pattern, the lines were assigned to the $J = 2\rightarrow1$, $3\rightarrow2$, $5\rightarrow4$, and $6\rightarrow5$ transitions of \ce{HCS^+} at 85, 128, 213, and 256~GHz, respectively. The confirming laboratory measurements were presented in a companion letter by \citet{Gudeman:1981:L47}.

name: hydroxymethyliumylidene
label: mol:HOC+
note: *Confirmed in 1995 ApJ 455, L73
latex_body: \ce{HOC^+} was reported by \citet{Woods:1983:583} in FCRAO and Onsala observations toward Sgr B2.  The $J = 1\rightarrow0$ transition at 89478~MHz was identified based on the laboratory work of \citet{Gudeman:1982:1344}.  The detection was confirmed by \citet{Ziurys:1995:L73} who observed the $J = 2\rightarrow1$, and $3\rightarrow2$ transitions at 179 and 268~GHz, respectively.

name: silacyclopropynylidene
label: mol:c-SiC2
latex_body: \citet{Thaddeus:1984:L45} reported the detection of \ce{c-SiC2} in NRAO 36-ft and Bell 7-m telescope observations of IRC+10216.  Nine transitions between 93--171~GHz were observed and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Michalopoulos:1984:3556} who derived rotational constants from rotationally resolved optical transitions.  \citet{Thaddeus:1984:L45} note that a number of these transitions had previously been observed in IRC+10216 and classified as unidentified by various other researchers as early as 1976. \citet{Suenram:1989:L103} and \citet{Gottlieb:1989:L29} subsequently reported the laboratory observation of the pure rotational spectrum. \ce{c-SiC2} was the first molecular ring molecule identified in the ISM.

events.summary: Restored cyclic SiC2 identity in label and table formula.

name: dicarbon sulfide
label: mol:C2S
note: *Also Cernicharo et al. 1987 A&A 181, L9
latex_body: The detection of \ce{C2S} ($^3\Sigma ^-$) was reported toward TMC-1 and Sgr B2 by \citet{Saito:1987:L115} using the Nobeyama 45-m telescope.  The laboratory measurements were also performed by \citet{Saito:1987:L115}. Although published a month earlier than \citet{Saito:1987:L115}, \citet{Cernicharo:1987:L9} reported the detection of \ce{C2S} in IRC+10216 using the laboratory results of \citet{Saito:1987:L115} from a preprint article.

name: tricarbon
label: mol:C3
latex_body: \citet{Hinkle:1988:1319} reported the detection of \ce{C3} in KPNO 4-m telescope observations of IRC+10216.  The $\nu_3$ band of \ce{C3} was observed and assigned based on combination differences from the work of \citet{Gausset:1965:45} near 2030~cm$^{-1}$.

name: carbon dioxide
label: mol:CO2
note: *First detected in ices, then in gas phase
latex_body: \citet{DHendecourt:1989:L5} reported the observation of the $\nu_2$ bending mode of \ce{CO2} ice in absorption at 15.2~$\mu$m using archival spectra from the IRAS database toward AFGL 961, AFGL 989, and AFGL 890.  The assignment was based on laboratory spectroscopy of mixed \ce{CO2} ices \citep{DHendecourt:1986:453}. Gas-phase \ce{CO2} was later observed toward numerous sightlines with ISO as a sharp absorption feature near 15~$\mu$m superimposed on a broad solid-phase absorption feature near the same frequency \citep{vanDishoeck:1996:L349}.  The frequencies were obtained from \citet{Paso:1980:236}, while the band strengths used were taken from \citet{Reichle:1972:2662}.

events.summary: Detected in exoplanetary atmosphere; 13CO2 in protoplanetary disks

name: methylene
label: mol:CH2
note: *Confirmed in 1995 ApJ 438, 259
latex_body: \ce{CH2} was first detected by \citet{Hollis:1989:794} in NRAO 12-m telescope observations of Orion.  Several hyperfine components of $N_{K_a,K_c} = 4_{0,4}\rightarrow3_{1,3}$ transition were observed at 68 and 71~GHz and were assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Lovas:1983:L131}.  The detection was later confirmed by \citet{Hollis:1995:259}.

name: dicarbon monoxide
label: mol:C2O
latex_body: The detection of \ce{C2O} was reported by \citet{Ohishi:1991:L39} toward TMC-1 using the Nobeyama 45-m telescope.  The $N_J = 1_2\rightarrow0_1$ and $2_3\rightarrow1_2$ transitions at 22 and 46~GHz, respectively, were assigned based on the laboratory data of \citet{Yamada:1985:L65}.

name: magnesium isocyanide
label: mol:MgNC
note: *Actually identified in Kawaguchi et al. 1993 ApJ 406, L39 and Guélin et al. 1993 A&A 280, L19
latex_body: \citet{Kawaguchi:1993:L39} successfully assigned a series of three, unidentified harmonically spaced doublet emission lines detected by \citet{Guelin:1986:L17} in IRAM 30-m observations of IRC+10216 to the $N = 7\rightarrow6$, $8\rightarrow7$, and $9\rightarrow8$ transitions of MgNC based on their own laboratory spectroscopy of the species.  MgNC was the first magnesium-containing molecule to be detected in the ISM.

name: amidogen
label: mol:NH2
latex_body: The detection of \ce{NH2} was reported by \citet{vanDishoeck:1993:L83} toward Sgr B2 using CSO observations of five components of the $J = 3/2\rightarrow3/2$, $1/2\rightarrow1/2$, and $3/2\rightarrow1/2$ transitions at 426, 469, and 461~GHz, respectively, based on the laboratory work of \citet{Burkholder:1988:415} and \citet{Charo:1981:L111}.  Some hyperfine splitting was resolved.

name: sodium cyanide
label: mol:NaCN
latex_body: The detection of NaCN was reported by \citet{Turner:1994:L97} using NRAO 12-m telescope observations of IRC+10216.  The $J_{K_a,K_c} = 5_{0,5}\rightarrow4_{0,4}$, $6_{0,6}\rightarrow5_{0,5}$, $7_{0,7}\rightarrow6_{0,6}$, and $9_{0,9}\rightarrow8_{0,8}$ transitions at 78, 93, 108, and 139~GHz, respectively, were observed.  The assignments were based on predictions from the rotational constants derived in \citet{vanVaals:1984:147}.

name: nitrous oxide
label: mol:N2O
latex_body: \citet{Ziurys:1994:L181} reported the detection of the $J = 3\rightarrow2$, $4\rightarrow3$, $5\rightarrow4$, and $6\rightarrow5$ transitions of \ce{N2O} at 75, 100, 125, and 150~GHz, respectively, in NRAO 12-m observations toward Sgr B2.  The laboratory frequencies were obtained from \citet{Lovas:1978:1445}.

name: magnesium cyanide
label: mol:MgCN

dipole.note: Ziurys:1995:L47 indicates that the dipole moment comes from a private communication from P. Valiron and was calculated at the UMP2F-6311+63 df level.

latex_body: The detection of the MgCN radical was reported by \citet{Ziurys:1995:L47} in NRAO 12-m and IRAM 30-m observations of IRC+10216.  The $N = 11\rightarrow10$, $10\rightarrow9$, and $9\rightarrow8$ transitions were observed, some with resolved spin-rotation splitting, based on the accompanying laboratory work of \citet{Anderson:1994:L41}.

events.summary: Replaced placeholder dipole moment with Ziurys et al. 1995 private-communication computed MgCN mu_a value.

name: Trihydrogen ion
label: mol:H3+
latex_body: First suggested as a possible interstellar molecule in \citet{Martin:1961:1012}, \ce{H3+} was detected 35 years later in absorption toward GL 2136 and W33A by \citet{Geballe:1996:334} using UKIRT to observe three transitions of the $\nu_2$ fundamental band near 3.7~$\mu$m.  The laboratory work was performed by \citet{Oka:1980:531}.

name: silicon monocyanide radical
label: mol:SiCN
latex_body: \citet{Guelin:2000:L9} reported the detection of the SiCN radical in IRAM 30-m observations of IRC+10216.  Three $\Lambda$-doubled transitions at 83, 94, and 105~GHz were detected based on the laboratory work by \citet{Apponi:2000:L55}.

name: aluminum isocyanide
label: mol:AlNC
latex_body: The detection of AlNC toward IRC+10216 with the IRAM 30-m telescope was reported by \citet{Ziurys:2002:L45}.  Five transitions between 132--251~GHz were assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Robinson:1997:1}.

name: silicon monoisocyanide
label: mol:SiNC
latex_body: \citet{Guelin:2004:L49} reported the detection of the SiNC radical in IRAM 30-m telescope observations of IRC+10216.  Four rotational transitions between 83--134~GHz were observed and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Apponi:2000:L55}.

name: phosphaethyne
label: mol:HCP
note: *First attempt 1990 ApJ 365, 59. Confirmed 2008 ApJ 684, 618
latex_body: \citet{Agundez:2007:L91} reported the detection of four transitions ($J = 4\rightarrow3$ through $7\rightarrow6$) of HCP toward IRC+10216 using the IRAM 30-m telescope.  The enabling laboratory work was performed by \citet{Bizzocchi:2001:110} and references therein.

name: dicarbon phosphide radical
label: mol:CCP
latex_body: The detection of the CCP radical in ARO 12-m observations of IRC+10216 was reported by \citet{Halfen:2008:L101}.  Five transitions with  partially resolved hyperfine splitting were identified and assigned based on laboratory work described in the same manuscript.

name: aluminum hydroxide
label: mol:AlOH
latex_body: AlOH was detected in ARO 12-m and SMT observations of VY Canis Majoris by \citet{Tenenbaum:2010:L93}. The $J = 9\rightarrow8$, $7\rightarrow6$, and $5\rightarrow4$ transitions at 283, 220, and 157~GHz, respectively, were identified based on the enabling laboratory work of \citet{Apponi:1993:L129}.

name: oxidaniumyl
label: mol:H2O+
latex_body: \ce{H2O^+} was identified in \emph{Herschel}/HIFI spectra toward DR21, Sgr B2, and NGC 6334 by \citet{Ossenkopf:2010:L111}.  Six hyperfine components of the $N_{K_a,K_c} = 1_{1,1}\rightarrow0_{0,0}$, $J = 3/2\rightarrow1/2$ transition in the $^2B_1$ electronic ground state at 1.115~THz were observed.  The assignments were based on a synthesis, re-analysis, and extrapolation of the laboratory work by \citet{Strahan:1986:1252} and \citet{Murtz:1998:9744}  Nearly simultaneously, \citet{Gerin:2010:L110} reported the observation of \ce{H2O+} along the line of sight to W31C, also using \emph{Herschel}/HIFI.

name: chloronium
label: mol:H2Cl+
latex_body: \citet{Lis:2010:L9} reported the observation of the $J_{K_a,K_c} = 2_{1,2}\rightarrow1_{0,1}$ transitions of \emph{ortho}-\ce{H2^{35}Cl^+} and \emph{ortho}-\ce{H2^{37}Cl^+} near 781~GHz, and the $J_{K_a,K_c} = 1_{1,1}\rightarrow0_{0,0}$ transition of \emph{para}-\ce{H2^{35}Cl^+} near 485~GHz in absorption toward NGC 6334I and Sgr B2 using \emph{Herschel}/HIFI.  The frequencies were derived from the rotational constants determined in the laboratory work of \citet{Araki:2001:132}.

name: potassium cyanide
label: mol:KCN
latex_body: The detection of KCN was reported by \citet{Pulliam:2010:L181} using ARO 12-m, IRAM 30-m, and SMT observations of IRC+10216.  More than a dozen transitions between 85--250~GHz were assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Torring:1980:4875}.

name: iron cyanide
label: mol:FeCN
latex_body: \citet{Zack:2011:L36} reported the detection of six transitions of FeCN between 84--132~GHz in ARO 12-m observations of IRC+10216.  The enabling laboratory spectroscopy was reported in \citet{Flory:2011:184303}, which was not yet published at the time of the publication of \citet{Zack:2011:L36}.

name: hydroperoxyl radical
label: mol:HO2
latex_body: The detection of \ce{HO2} was reported in IRAM 30-m and APEX observations toward $\rho$ Oph A by \citet{Parise:2012:L11}.  Several hyperfine components were observed in the $N_{K_a,K_c} = 2_{0,2}\rightarrow1_{0,1}$ and $4_{0,4}\rightarrow3_{0,3}$ transitions at 130 and 261~GHz, respectively.  The laboratory work was performed by \citet{Beers:1975:4212}, \citet{Saito:1977:229}, and \citet{Charo:1982:426}.

name: titanium dioxide
label: mol:TiO2
latex_body: \ce{TiO2} was detected by \citet{Kaminski:2013:A113} in SMA and PdBI observations of VY Canis Majoris.  More than two dozen transitions of \ce{TiO2} were observed between 221--351~GHz based on the laboratory work of \citet{Brunken:2008:1367} and \citet{Kania:2011:173}.

name: cyanomethylidyne
label: mol:CCN
latex_body: \citet{Anderson:2014:L1} reported the detection of CCN in ARO 12-m and SMT observations of IRC+10216.  The $J = 9/2\rightarrow7/2$, $13/2\rightarrow11/2$, and $19/2\rightarrow17/2$ $\Lambda$-doubled transitions near 106, 154, and 225~GHz, respectively, were identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Anderson:2015:1} which was published several months later.

name: disilicon carbide
label: mol:SiCSi
latex_body: 112 transitions of SiCSi were observed in IRAM 30-m telescope observations of IRC+10216 between 80--350~GHz as reported by \citet{Miyatake:2015:1}.  The transition frequencies were derived based on the contemporaneous laboratory work of \citet{McCarthy:2015:2107}.

name: hydrogen disulfide
label: mol:S2H
latex_body: \citet{Fuente:2017:L49} reported the detection of \ce{S2H} in IRAM 30-m observations of the Horsehead PDR region.  Although \citet{Fuente:2017:L49} do not not provide quantum numbers, they detect four lines corresponding to the unresolved hyperfine doublets of the $J_{K_a,K_c} = 6_{0,6}\rightarrow5_{0,5}$ and $7_{0,7}\rightarrow6_{0,6}$ transitions near 94 and 110~GHz, respectively.  The laboratory analysis was described in \citet{Tanimoto:2000:73}.

name: thioformyl
label: mol:HCS
latex_body: The detection of HCS was reported by \citet{Agundez:2018:L1} in IRAM 30-m observations of L483.  Five resolved hyperfine components of the $N_{K_a,K_c} = 2_{0,2}\rightarrow1_{0,1}$ transition of HCS near 81~GHz were identified based on the laboratory work of \citet{Habara:2002:9232}.

name: sulfhydryl carbide
label: mol:HSC
latex_body: The detection of HSC was reported by \citet{Agundez:2018:L1} in IRAM 30-m observations of L483.  Two resolved hyperfine components of the $N_{K_a,K_c} = 2_{0,2}\rightarrow1_{0,1}$ transition of HSC near 81~GHz were identified based on the laboratory work of \citet{Habara:2000:10905}.

name: isocyanate radical
label: mol:NCO
latex_body: \citet{Marcelino:2018:L10} reported the detection of the NCO radical in IRAM 30-m observations of L483.  Several hyperfine components of the $J = 7/2\rightarrow5/2$ and $9/2\rightarrow7/2$ transitions near 81.4 and 104.6~GHz were identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Saito:1970:383} and \citet{Kawaguchi:1985:341}.

name: calcium isocyanide
label: mol:CaNC
note: Dipole moment from Steimle et al. 1992 JCP 97, 2909
latex_body: \citet{Cernicharo:2019:L4} reported the detection of CaNC in IRAM 30-m observations of IRC+10216, the first calcium-bearing molecule detected in interstellar or circumstellar media.   A total of nine doublets between 72.9--169.9\,GHz corresponding to transitions between $N=9\rightarrow8$ and $N=21\rightarrow20$, some severely blended, were identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Steimle:1993:L49} and \citet{Scurlock:1994:3497}, and using a dipole moment from \citet{Steimle:1992:2909}.

name: thiocyanogen
label: mol:NCS
note: Dipole moment taken from CDMS as calculated by Holger Müller.  Amano & Amano point out that this calculation shoudl be quite challenging, and neither of the more recent laboratory papers appears to perform it, so this value should be viewed with caution.

name: magnesium dicarbide
label: mol:MgC2
note: Dipole moment from Itono et al. 2000 ApJ 538, L163.  Detection is of 24MgC2 (main isotopologue) as well as 25MgC2 and 26MgC2.

name: HSO radical
label: mol:HSO
note: Suggestions for the appropriate chemical name for this species are welcome.

name: ammonia
label: mol:NH3
latex_body: The first detection of \ce{NH3} was reported by \citet{Cheung:1968:1701} by observation of its ($J,K$) = (1,1) and (2,2) inversion transitions in the Galactic Center using a 20-m radio telescope located at Hat Creek Observatory.  No references to the laboratory data are given, but the frequencies were likely derived from the accumulated works of \citet{Cleeton:1934:234}, \citet{Gunther-Mohr:1954:1184}, \citet{Kukolich:1965:1322}, and \citet{Kukolich:1967:83}.

name: formaldehyde
label: mol:H2CO
latex_body: \citet{Snyder:1969:679} reported the detection of \ce{H2CO} in NRAO 140-ft telescope observations of more than a dozen interstellar sources.  The $J_{K_a,K_c} = 1_{1,1}\rightarrow1_{1,0}$ transition at 4830~MHz was observed without hyperfine splitting, based on the laboratory data of \citet{Shigenari:1967:404}.

name: isocyanic acid
label: mol:HNCO
latex_body: HNCO was observed in NRAO 36-ft observations of Sgr B2 by \citet{Snyder:1972:619}.  The $J_{K_a,K_c} = 4_{0,4}\rightarrow3_{0,3}$ transition at 87925~MHz was detected and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Kewley:1963:418}.  The detection was confirmed in a companion article with the observation of the $1_{0,1}\rightarrow0_{0,0}$ transition by \citet{Buhl:1972:625}.

name: thioformaldehyde
label: mol:H2CS
latex_body: \citet{Sinclair:1973:85} reported the detection of \ce{H2CS} through Parkes 64-m observations of the Sgr B2.  The $J_{K_a,K_c} = 2_{1,1}\rightarrow2_{1,2}$ transition at 3139~MHz was identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Johnson:1970:679}.

name: acetylene
label: mol:C2H2
latex_body: The detection of \ce{C2H2} was reported by \citet{Ridgway:1976:345} in Mayall 4-m telescope observations of IRC+10216.  The $\nu_1 + \nu_5$ combination band of acetylene at 4091~cm$^{-1}$ was identified based on the laboratory work of \citet{Baldacci:1973:600}.

name: cyanoethynyl radical
label: mol:C3N
note: *Confirmed in Friberg et al. 1980 ApJ 241, L99
latex_body: \citet{Guelin:1977:L81} reported the tentative detection of \ce{C3N} in NRAO 36-ft observations of IRC+10216.  They observed two sets of doublet transitions, with the center frequencies at 89 and 99~GHz.  Based on calculated rotational constants, they tentatively assigned the emission to \ce{C3N}. \citet{Friberg:1980:L99} later confirmed the detection by observing the predicted $N  = 3\rightarrow2$ transitions near 30~GHz.  The laboratory spectra were subsequently measured by \citet{Gottlieb:1983:916}.

name: isothiocyanic acid
label: mol:HNCS

dipole.note: Szalanski:1978:1297 reports mu_a = 1.64 D and mu_b = 1.0 D for HNCS.

latex_body: HNCS was detected by observation of the $J = 11\rightarrow10$, $9\rightarrow8$, and $8\rightarrow7$ transitions, among others, at 192, 106, and 94~GHz, respectively, in Bell 7-m and NRAO 36-ft telescope observations of Sgr B2 by \citet{Frerking:1979:L143}.  The laboratory frequencies were measured by \citet{Kewley:1963:418}.

events.summary: Replaced placeholder dipole component with Szalanski et al. 1978 HNCS mu_a and mu_b values.

name: protonated carbon dioxide
label: mol:HOCO+
latex_body: \citet{Thaddeus:1981:L41} reported the observation of a series of three lines in Bell 7-m observations of Sgr B2 they assigned to the $J = 6\rightarrow5$, $5\rightarrow4$, and $4\rightarrow3$ transitions of \ce{HOCO+} at 128, 107, and 86~GHz, respectively, based on \emph{ab initio} calculations by \citet{Green:1976:479}.  The detection was later confirmed by laboratory observation of the rotational spectrum by \citet{Bogey:1984:L11}.

name: tricarbon monoxide
label: mol:C3O
note: *Confirmed in Brown et al. 1985 ApJ 297, 302 and Kaifu et al. 2004 PASJ 56, 69
latex_body: The detection of \ce{C3O} was reported by \citet{Matthews:1984:125} through NRAO 140-ft telescope observations of TMC-1.  The $J = 2\rightarrow1$ transition at 19244~MHz was observed and assigned based on laboratory work by \citet{Brown:1983:6496}.  Three further transitions up to $J = 9\rightarrow8$ were observed in a follow-up study in the same source by \citet{Brown:1985:302}. The detection was confirmed by \citet{Kaifu:2004:69} with the observation of numerous additional lines in Nobeyama 45-m observations of TMC-1.

name: propynylidyne radical
label: mol:l-C3H
latex_body: The $l$-\ce{C3H} radical was detected toward TMC-1 and IRC+10216 through a combination of observations with the Bell 7-m, University of Massachusetts 14-m, NRAO 36-ft, and Onsala 20-m telescopes as reported in \citet{Thaddeus:1985:L49}.  A number of transitions between 33--103~GHz were identified based on the accompanying laboratory work of \citet{Gottlieb:1985:L55}.

name: protonated hydrogen cyanide
label: mol:HCNH+
latex_body: \ce{HCNH^+} was reported in NRAO 12-m and MWO 4.9-m telescope observations of Sgr B2 by \citet{Ziurys:1986:L31}.  The $J = 1\rightarrow0$, $2\rightarrow1$, and $3\rightarrow2$ transitions were targeted at 74, 148, and 222~GHz, respectively, based on frequencies estimated from the laboratory work of \citet{Altman:1984:3911} and confirmed during the course of publication by the laboratory work of \citet{Bogey:1985:3703}.

name: hydronium
label: mol:H3O+
note: *Confirmed in Wootten et al. 1991 ApJ 390, L79
latex_body: \citet{Wootten:1986:L15} and \citet{Hollis:1986:524} nearly simultaneously reported the detection of \ce{H3O^+}.  \citet{Wootten:1986:L15} used the NRAO 12-m telescope to search for the $J_K = 1_1\rightarrow2_1$ transition at 307.2~GHz in Orion and Sgr B2, reporting a detection in each.  \citet{Hollis:1986:524} also observed the same transition in both Orion and Sgr B2 with the NRAO 12-m telescope.  Later, \citet{Wootten:1991:L79} reported the detection of a confirming line in Orion and Sgr B2 with the identification of the $3_2\rightarrow2_2$ transition of \emph{ortho}-\ce{H3O^+} using the CSO.   These detections were based on the laboratory work of \citet{Plummer:1985:1428}, \citet{Bogey:1985:L11}, and \citet{Liu:1985:1787}.

name: tricarbon monosulfide
label: mol:C3S
latex_body: The detection of \ce{C3S} was reported by \citet{Yamamoto:1987:L119}.  The authors measured the laboratory rotational spectrum of the molecule, and assigned the $^1\Sigma$ $J = 4\rightarrow3$, $7\rightarrow6$, and $8\rightarrow7$ lines at 23, 40, and 46~GHz, respectively to previously unidentified lines in the observations of \citet{Kaifu:1987:L111} toward TMC-1 using the Nobeyama 45-m telescope.

name: cyclopropenylidene radical
label: mol:c-C3H
latex_body: \citet{Yamamoto:1987:L55} reported the detection of the hyperfine components of the $J = 5/2\rightarrow3/2$ and $3/2\rightarrow1/2$ transitions at 91.5 and 91.7~GHz, respectively, in Nobeyama 45-m observations of TMC-1.  The enabling laboratory spectroscopy was presented in the same manuscript.

name: cyanocarbene radical
label: mol:HC2N
latex_body: \citet{Guelin:1991:L21} reported the detection of nine lines of \ce{HC2N} in IRAM 30-m observations of IRC+10216 between 72--239~GHz.  The enabling laboratory work was presented in \citet{Saito:1984:1427} and \citet{Brown:1990:203}.

name: methylene amidogen radical
label: mol:H2CN
latex_body: The detection of \ce{H2CN} was reported in NRAO 12-m observations of TMC-1 by \citet{Ohishi:1994:L51} who observed two hyperfine components of the $N_{K_a,K_c} = 1_{0,1}\rightarrow0_{0,0}$ transition at 73.3~GHz.  The laboratory spectroscopy was conducted by \citet{Yamamoto:1992:4157}.

name: silicon tricarbide
label: mol:SiC3
latex_body: \citet{Apponi:1999:L103} reported the detection of \ce{SiC3} in NRAO 12-m observations of IRC+10216.  Nine transitions of \ce{SiC3} between 81--103~GHz were observed and assigned based on laboratory work by the same group, published shortly thereafter in \citet{McCarthy:1999:10645} and \citet{Apponi:1999:3911}.

name: methyl radical
label: mol:CH3
latex_body: The detection of \ce{CH3} was reported by \citet{Feuchtgruber:2000:L111} using ISO observations of the $\nu_2$ $Q$-branch line at 16.5~$\mu$m and the $R(0)$ line at 16.0~$\mu$m toward Sgr~A*.  The enabling laboratory work was performed by \citet{Yamada:1981:5256}.  The first ground-based detection of \ce{CH3} was described later by \citet{Knez:2009:471}.

name: cyanoethynyl anion
label: mol:C3N-
latex_body: Both the laboratory spectroscopy and astronomical detection of \ce{C3N^-} were presented in \citet{Thaddeus:2008:1132}.  The anion was detected in IRAM 30-m observations of IRC+10216 in the $J = 10\rightarrow9$, $11\rightarrow10$, $14\rightarrow13$, and $15\rightarrow14$ transitions at 97, 107, 136, and 146~GHz, respectively.

name: phosphine
label: mol:PH3
note: *Confirmed in Agúndez et al. 2014 ApJL 790, L27
latex_body: \citet{Agundez:2008:L33} and \citet{Tenenbaum:2008:L121} simultaneously and independently reported the tentative detection of \ce{PH3}.  \citet{Tenenbaum:2008:L121} observed emission from the $J_K = 1_0\rightarrow0_0$ transition at 267~GHz toward IRC+10216 and CRL~2688 using the SMT telescope.  \citet{Agundez:2008:L33} observed the same transition toward IRC+10216 using the IRAM 30-m telescope, and searched for the $J = 3\rightarrow2$ transition at 801~GHz using the CSO, unsuccessfully.  These detections were confirmed by \citet{Agundez:2014:L27} through successful observation of the 534~GHz $J = 2\rightarrow1$ line toward IRC+10216 with \emph{Herschel}/HIFI.  The laboratory spectroscopy was presented in \citet{Cazzoli:2006:64}, \citet{Sousa-Silva:2013:28}, and \citet{Muller:2013:335}.

name: fulminic acid
label: mol:HCNO
latex_body: The discovery of HCNO was reported by \citet{Marcelino:2009:L27} through observation of the $J = 5\rightarrow4$ and $4\rightarrow3$ transitions at 92 and 115~GHz, respectively, in IRAM 30-m observations of TMC-1, L1527, B1-b, L1544, and L183.  The laboratory rotational spectra were reported in \citet{Winnewisser:1971:128}.

name: cyanic acid
label: mol:HOCN
note: *Confirmed in Brünken et al. 2010 A&A 516, A109
latex_body: The laboratory rotational spectrum and tentative astronomical identification of HOCN was reported by \citet{Brunken:2009:880} toward Sgr B2 using archival survey data.  The $J_{K_a,K_c} = 5_{0,5}\rightarrow4_{0,4}$ and $6_{0,6}\rightarrow5_{0,5}$ transitions at 104.9 and 125.8~GHz, respectively, were observed in Bell 7-m observations by \citet{Cummins:1986:819}. The $4_{0,4}\rightarrow3_{0,3}$ transition at 83.9~GHz was observed in the survey of \citet{Turner:1989:539} using the NRAO 36-ft telescope, but mis-assigned in that work to a transition of \ce{CH3OD}. These detections were confirmed shortly thereafter by \citet{Brunken:2010:A109} using IRAM 30-m observations of Sgr B2 to self-consistently observe the $4_{0,4}\rightarrow3_{0,3}$ through $8_{0,8}\rightarrow7_{0,7}$ transitions.

name: thiocyanic acid
label: mol:HSCN
latex_body: \citet{Halfen:2009:L124} reported the detection of HSCN in ARO 12-m observations of Sgr B2.  Six lines between 69--138~GHz were observed and assigned to the $J_{K_a,K_c} = 6_{0,6}\rightarrow5_{0,5}$ through $12_{0,12}\rightarrow11_{0,11}$ transitions based on the laboratory work of \citet{Brunken:2009:1588}.

name: hydrogen peroxide
label: mol:HOOH
latex_body: The detection of HOOH was reported by \citet{Bergman:2011:L8} in APEX 12-m observations toward $\rho$ Oph A.  Three lines corresponding to the $J_{K_a,K_c} = 3_{0,3}\rightarrow2_{1,1}$ $\tau = 4\rightarrow2$, $6_{1,5}\rightarrow5_{0,5}$ $2\rightarrow4$, and $5_{0,5}\rightarrow4_{1,3}$ $4\rightarrow2$ torsion-rotation transitions at 219, 252, and 318~GHz, respectively, were assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Helminger:1981:120} and \citet{Petkie:1995:145}.

name: propynylidyne cation
label: mol:l-C3H+
latex_body: \citet{Pety:2012:A68} first reported the detection of a series of eight harmonically spaced unidentified lines in IRAM 30-m observations of the Horsehead PDR region which seemed to correspond to the $J = 4\rightarrow3$ through $12\rightarrow11$ transitions of a linear or quasi-linear molecule.  Based on the comparison of their derived rotational constants to \emph{ab initio} values calculated by \citet{Ikuta:1997:4536}, they tentatively assigned the carrier of these lines to the $l$-\ce{C3H^+} cation.  Using the derived spectroscopic parameters, \citet{McGuire:2013:56} subsequently detected the $1\rightarrow0$ and $2\rightarrow1$ transitions at 22.5 and 45~GHz, respectively, in absorption toward Sgr B2 using the GBT 100-m telescope.  Contemporaneously, \citet{Huang:2013:L25} and \citet{Fortenberry:2013:39} challenged the attribution to $l$-\ce{C3H^+}, suggesting that the \ce{C3H^-} anion was a more likely candidate, based on better agreement between the distortion constants from their high-level quantum chemical calculations to those derived by \citet{Pety:2012:A68}.  This assertion was challenged by \citet{McGuire:2014:36}, who argued that the formation and destruction chemistry in the high-UV environments the molecule was found strongly favored $l$-\ce{C3H+} over \ce{C3H^-}.  The assignment to $l$-\ce{C3H+} was shortly thereafter confirmed by the laboratory observation and characterization of the rotational spectrum of the cation by \citet{Brunken:2014:L4}.

events.summary: Corrected error in name (was duplicating cC3Hp)

name: hydromagnesium isocyanide
label: mol:HMgNC
latex_body: \citet{Cabezas:2013:133} reported the laboratory and astronomical identification of HMgNC in IRAM 30-m observations of IRC+10216. The $J = 8\rightarrow7$ through $13\rightarrow12$ transitions between 88 and 142~GHz were observed and assigned based on predicted values from the laboratory observations of the hyperfine-split $1\rightarrow0$ and $2\rightarrow1$ transitions at 11 and 22~GHz, respectively.

name: ketenyl radical
label: mol:HCCO
latex_body: The detection of HCCO was reported by \citet{Agundez:2015:L5} using IRAM 30-m observations of Lupus-1A and L483.  Four fine and hyperfine components of the $N = 4\rightarrow3$ transition of HCCO were resolved near 86.7~GHz and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Endo:1987:4319} and \citet{Ohshima:1993:458}.

name: isocyanogen
label: mol:CNCN
latex_body: \citet{Agundez:2018:L22} reported the detection of \ce{CNCN} in L483 using IRAM 30-m observations.  The $J = 8\rightarrow7$, $9\rightarrow8$, $10\rightarrow9$ transitions at 82.8, 93.1, and 103.5~GHz were observed and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Winnewisser:1992:635} and \citet{Gerry:1990:147}.  A tentative detection in TMC-1 was also reported in the same work.

name: nitrous acid
label: mol:HONO
note: Only lines of trans-HONO are claimed as detected. As such, constants for this entry are for trans-HONO.
latex_body: \citet{Coutens:2019:L13} reported the detection of \ce{HONO} in IRAS 16293 using ALMA observations.  Twelve lines between 329 -- 362 GHz were observed and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Guilmot:1993:401,Guilmot:1993:387} and \citet{Dehayem-Kamadjeu:2005:182}.

name: magnesium ethynyl radical
label: mol:MgCCH
note: Dipole from Woon 1996 ApJ 456, 602
latex_body: \citet{Agundez:2014:A45} reported the tentative detection of \ce{MgCCH} in IRAM 30-m observations of IRC+10216.  They identified and assigned two sets of features corresponding to $l$-doubled transitions of the $^2\Sigma ^+$ ground electronic state of \ce{MgCCH} at 89 and 99~GHz based on the laboratory work of \citet{Brewster:1999:411}. The detection was confirmed in \citet{Cernicharo:2019:L2} using IRAM 30-m and Yebes 40-m observations of the same source.

name: thioketenyl radical
label: mol:HCCS
note: Dipole moment is from Vrtilek et al. who in turn got it from J. D. Goddard 1992, private communication.

name: cyanomidyl radical
label: mol:HNCN
note: Dipole moment from CDMS.

name: aminocarbyne
label: mol:H2NC
note: No laboratory work; purely theoretical constants.

name: thioketenylium
label: mol:HCCS+
note: Identification performed based on quantum chemical calculations only.  Cabezas et al. do not state what dipole moment they assumed, but it was presumably taken from Puzzarini 2008 Chem Phys 346, 45

name: methylium
label: mol:CH3+
note: B and C constants are quite uncertain

name: protonated carbonyl sulfide
label: mol:HOCS+
note: Dipole from Wheeler et al. 2006 JCP 124, 044322

name: cyanoacetylene
label: mol:HC3N
note: *Confirmed in Dickinson 1972 AL 12, 235
latex_body: \citet{Turner:1971:L35} reported the detection of the $F = 2\rightarrow1$ and $1\rightarrow1$ hyperfine components of the $J = 1\rightarrow0$ transition of \ce{HC3N} at 9098 and 9097~MHz, respectively, in NRAO 140-ft telescope observations of Sgr B2.  The assignment was based on the laboratory work of \citet{Tyler:1963:2661}.  The detection was confirmed the following year by \citet{Dickinson:1972:235} through observation of two hyperfine components of the $J = 2\rightarrow1$ transition at 18~GHz in Haystack Observatory 120-ft telescope observations of Sgr B2.

name: formic acid
label: mol:HCOOH
note: *Confirmed in Winnewisser & Churchwell 1975 ApJ 200, L33
latex_body: The detection of HCOOH was reported by \citet{Zuckerman:1971:L41} in Sgr B2 using the NRAO 140-ft telescope.  The $J_{K_a,K_c} = 1_{1,1}\rightarrow1_{1,0}$ transition at 1639~MHz was identified and assigned based on laboratory work presented in the same manuscript.  Later, \citet{Winnewisser:1975:L33} confirmed the detection by observation of the $2_{1,1}\rightarrow2_{1,2}$ transition at 4.9~GHz in Sgr B2 using the MPIfR 100-m telescope.  This identification was based on the laboratory work of \citet{Bellet:1971:49} and \citet{Bellet:1971:65} (in French).

name: methanimine
label: mol:CH2NH
latex_body: \citet{Godfrey:1973:119} reported the detection of \ce{CH2NH} in Sgr B2 using the Parkes 64-m telescope.  The $J = 1_{1,0}\rightarrow1_{1,1}$ transition at 5.2~GHz was observed and assigned based on laboratory work presented in the same manuscript, and building on the earlier laboratory efforts of \citet{Johnson:1972:65}.  \ce{CH2NH} is also referred to as methylenimine.

name: cyanamide
label: mol:NH2CN
latex_body: \citet{Turner:1975:L149} described the detection of \ce{NH2CN} in Sgr B2 by observation of its $J_{K_a,K_c} = 5_{1,4}\rightarrow4_{1,3}$ and $4_{1,3}\rightarrow3_{1,2}$ transitions at 100.6 and 80.5~GHz, respectively, using the NRAO 36-foot telescope.  The assignment was based on the work of \citet{Lide:1962:142}, \citet{Millen:1962:153}, and \citet{Tyler:1972:248}, and subsequently confirmed in the laboratory by \citet{Johnson:1976:245}.

name: ketene
label: mol:H2CCO
latex_body: The detection of \ce{H2CCO} was reported by \citet{Turner:1977:L75} in NRAO 36-foot telescope observations of Sgr B2.  The $J_{K_a,K_c} = 5_{1,4}\rightarrow4_{1,3}$, $5_{1,5}\rightarrow4_{1,4}$, and $4_{1,3}\rightarrow3_{1,2}$ transitions at 102, 100, and 82~GHz, respectively, were observed and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Johnson:1952:687} and \citet{Johns:1972:523}.

name: butadiynyl radical
label: mol:C4H
latex_body: \citet{Guelin:1978:L27} reported the tentative detection of \ce{C4H} using NRAO 36-ft observations of IRC+10216 in combination with the previously published observations of \citet{Scoville:1978:L103} and \citet{Liszt:1978:454} in complementary frequency ranges.  In total, four sets of spin doublet lines were observed between 86--114~GHz, and assigned to the $N = 9\rightarrow8$ through $N = 12\rightarrow11$ transitions of \ce{C4H} based on comparison to the theoretical rotational constants calculated by \citet{Wilson:1977:L87}.  The detection was subsequently confirmed through the laboratory efforts of \citet{Gottlieb:1983:916}.

name: silane
label: mol:SiH4
latex_body: The detection of \ce{SiH4} was reported by \citet{Goldhaber:1984:L55} in IRTF observations toward IRC+10216.  Thirteen absorption lines in the $\nu_4$ band near 917~cm$^{-1}$ were assigned based on laboratory work described in the same manuscript.

name: cyclopropenylidene
label: mol:c-C3H2
note: *See also Vrtilek et al. 1987 ApJ 314, 716
latex_body: The laboratory spectroscopy and interstellar detection of \ce{c-C3H2} was described in a pair of papers by \citet{Thaddeus:1985:L63} and \citet{Vrtilek:1987:716}.  After the report of \citet{Thaddeus:1985:L63}, the molecule began to be detected in numerous sources, with the best detections, as reported in \citet{Vrtilek:1987:716} being in Sgr B2, Orion, and TMC-1 with the Bell 7-m telescope.  A total of 11 transitions between 18--267~GHz were initially assigned.

name: cyanomethyl radical
label: mol:CH2CN
latex_body: \citet{Irvine:1988:L107} reported the detection of the \ce{CH2CN} radical in TMC-1 and Sgr B2 using a combination of observations from the FCRAO 14-m, NRAO 140-ft, Onsala 20-m, and Nobeyama 45-m telescopes.  Numerous hyperfine-resolved components of the $N_{K_a,K_c} = 1_{0,1}\rightarrow0_{0,0}$ and $2_{0,2}\rightarrow1_{0,1}$ transitions at 20 and 40~GHz, respectively were observed in TMC-1, as well as an unresolved detection of the $4_{0,4}\rightarrow4_{0,3}$ transition at 101~GHz.  The assignments were made based on laboratory work presented in a companion paper from \citet{Saito:1988:L113}.  Five partially-resolved components were also detected in Sgr B2 between 40--101~GHz.

name: pentacarbon
label: mol:C5
latex_body: The detection of \ce{C5} was reported by \citet{Bernath:1989:562} in KPNO 4-m telescope observations of IRC+10216.  More than a dozen $P$- and $R$-branch transitions of the $\nu_3$ asymmetric stretching mode near 2164~cm$^{-1}$ were detected, guided by the laboratory work of \citet{Vala:1989:595}.

name: silicon tetracarbide
label: mol:SiC4
latex_body: \citet{Ohishi:1989:L83} reported the detection of \ce{SiC4} in Nobeyama 45-m observations of IRC+10216.  Their search was initially guided by quantum chemical calculations they carried out, the results of which led to the assignment of five astronomically observed features between 37--89~GHz to the $J = 12\rightarrow11$, $13\rightarrow12$, $14\rightarrow13$, $16\rightarrow15$, and $28\rightarrow27$ transitions of \ce{SiC4}.  In the same work, they confirmed the detection by conducting laboratory microwave spectroscopy of the $J = 42\rightarrow41$ through $48\rightarrow47$ transitions.

name: propadienylidene
label: mol:H2CCC
latex_body: The detection of \ce{H2CCC} was reported by \citet{Cernicharo:1991:L39} in IRAM 30-m telescope observations and archival Effelsberg 100-m telescope observations \citep{Cernicharo:1987:L1} of TMC-1.  The $J_{K_a,K_c} = 1_{0,1}\rightarrow0_{0,0}$ transition of \emph{para}-\ce{H2CCC} at 21~GHz, and three transitions of \emph{ortho}-\ce{H2CCC} between 103--147~GHz were identified based on the laboratory work of \citet{Vrtilek:1990:L53}.

name: methane
label: mol:CH4
latex_body: \ce{CH4} was detected in both the gas phase and solid phase in IRTF observations toward NGC 7538 IRS 9 by \citet{Lacy:1991:556}.  The gas-phase $R(0)$ line and two blended $R(2)$ lines at 1311.43, 1322.08, and 1322.16~cm$^{-1}$ were observed and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Champion:1989:256}.  The solid-phase absorption of the $\nu_4$ mode  near 7.7~$\mu$m was observed and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{DHendecourt:1986:453}.

events.summary: Added CH3D detection in exoplanetary atmosphere

name: isocyanoacetylene
label: mol:HCCNC
latex_body: \citet{Kawaguchi:1992:L51} reported the detection of \ce{HCCNC}, also known as isocyanoethyne and  ethynyl isocyanide, in Nobeyama 45-m observations of TMC-1.  The $J = 4\rightarrow3$, $5\rightarrow4$, and $9\rightarrow8$ transitions at 40, 50, and 89~GHz, respectively, were identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Guarnieri:1992:39}.

name: Iminopropadienylidene
label: mol:HNCCC
latex_body: \citet{Kawaguchi:1992:L49} reported both the laboratory spectroscopy and astronomical identification of HNCCC in Nobeyama 45-m telescope observations of TMC-1.  The $J = 3\rightarrow2$, $4\rightarrow3$, and $5\rightarrow4$ transitions at 28, 37, and 47~GHz, respectively, were assigned and identified.

name: protonated formaldehyde
label: mol:H2COH+
latex_body: The detection of \ce{H2COH^+} was reported by \citet{Ohishi:1996:L61} in Nobeyama 45-m and NRAO 12-m telescope observations of Sgr B2, Orion, and W51.  Six transitions between 32--174~GHz were observed and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Chomiak:1994:1078}.

name: butadiynyl anion
label: mol:C4H-
latex_body: \citet{Cernicharo:2007:L37} reported the detection of \ce{C4H^-} in IRAM 30-m observations of IRC+10216 through observation of five transitions between 84--140~GHz.  The detection was enabled by the laboratory work of \citet{Gupta:2007:L57}.

name: cyanoformaldehyde
label: mol:CNCHO
latex_body: \ce{CNCHO} was detected in GBT 100-m observations of Sgr B2(N) by \citet{Remijan:2008:L85}.  A total of seven transitions between 2.1 and 41~GHz were identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Bogey:1988:227} and \citet{Bogey:1995:344}.  \ce{CNCHO} is also referred to as formyl cyanide.

name: carbodiimide
label: mol:HNCNH
latex_body: \citet{McGuire:2012:L33} reported the detection of HNCNH in GBT 100-m observations of Sgr B2.  Four sets of transitions were identified to arise from maser action, while several other stronger transitions incapable of masing were not observed.  The assignments were made based on the laboratory work of \citet{Birk:1989:402}, \citet{Wagener:1995:323}, and \citet{Jabs:1997:77}.

name: methoxy radical
label: mol:CH3O
latex_body: The detection of \ce{CH3O} was reported in IRAM 30-m observations of B1-b by \citet{Cernicharo:2012:L43}. Several hyperfine components of the $N = 1\rightarrow0$ transition near 82.4~GHz were identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Endo:1984:122} and \citet{Momose:1988:5338}.  Components of the $2\rightarrow1$ transition are shown, but no frequency information is provided other than that the transitions are at 2~mm.

name: ammonium ion
label: mol:NH3D+
note: *Confirmed in Marcelino et al. 2018 A&A 612, L10
latex_body: The detection of \ce{NH3D^+} was reported toward Orion and B1-b in IRAM 30-m observations by \citet{Cernicharo:2013:L10}.  A single line with unresolved hyperfine structure was observed and assigned to the $J_K = 1_0\rightarrow0_0$ transition of \ce{NH3D^+} based on laboratory results presented in the same manuscript.  A companion article by \citet{Domenech:2013:L11} detailed the laboratory results.

name: protonated isocyanic acid
label: mol:H2NCO+
note: *See also Doménech et al. 2013 ApJ 77, L11
latex_body: \citet{Gupta:2013:L1} reported a tentative detection of \ce{H2NCO^+} in GBT 100-m observations of Sgr B2.  Based on laboratory work presented in the same manuscript, they identified and assigned the $J_{K_a,K_c} = 0_{0,0}\rightarrow1_{0,1}$ and $1_{1,0}\rightarrow2_{1,1}$ transitions of \emph{para}- and \emph{ortho}-\ce{H2NCO^+} at 20.2 and 40.8~GHz, respectively.  The detection was confirmed by \citet{Marcelino:2018:L10} in IRAM 30-m observations of L483.  They observed six additional transitions of \ce{H2NCO^+} between 80--116~GHz.

name: protonated cyanogen
label: mol:NCCNH+
latex_body: \citet{Agundez:2015:L10} reported the detection of \ce{NCCNH^+} in TMC-1 and L483 using IRAM 30-m and Yerbes 40-m observations.  The $J = 5\rightarrow4$ and $10\rightarrow9$ transitions at 44.3 and 88.8~GHz, respectively, were identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Amano:1991:2280} and \citet{Gottlieb:2000:1910}.

name: chloromethane
label: mol:CH3Cl
latex_body: \ce{CH3Cl}, also called methyl chloride, was detected in ALMA observations of IRAS 16293, and in ROSINA mass spectrometry measurements of comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko, by \citet{Fayolle:2017:703}.  Both the \ce{^{35}Cl} and \ce{^{37}Cl} isotopologues were detected through observation and assignment of the $J_K = 13_K\rightarrow12_K$ $K = 0$ to 4 transitions between 340--360~GHz.  The laboratory work was presented by \citet{Wlodarczak:1986:251}.

name: magnesium cyanoethynyl radical
label: mol:MgC3N
note: Assigned based entirely on quantum chemistry; no lab work.
latex_body: \citet{Cernicharo:2019:L2} reported the detection of \ce{MgC3N} in IRAM 30-m and Yebes 40-m observations of IRC+10216.  A series of doublet lines between 33--111\,GHz were identified and assigned based on quantum chemical calculations.  To date, there has been no laboratory confirmation of these assignments.

name: protonated tricarbon monoxide
label: mol:HC3O+
latex_body: The detection of \ce{HC3O+} was reported by \citet{Cernicharo:2020:L17} in IRAM 30-m and Yebes 40-m observations of TMC-1.  They identify and assign four lines in their spectra to the $J = 4\rightarrow3$, $J = 5\rightarrow4$, $J = 10\rightarrow9$, and $J = 11\rightarrow10$ transitions between {35.6--98.1}\,GHz.  The initial assignment was based on quantum chemical calculations in the same paper, as well as from \citet{Thorwirth:2020:e1776409}.   Laboratory spectroscopy presented in the same paper confirms the detection.

name: hydroxylamine
label: mol:NH2OH
latex_body: \citet{Rivilla:2020:L28} reported the detection of \ce{NH2OH} in IRAM 30-m observations of G+0.693-0.027.  Based on the laboratory work of \citet{Tsunekawa:1972:167} and \citet{Morino:2000:367}, they identified and assigned approximately ten largely unblended rotational transitions between 100.7--201.6\,GHz.

name: protonated tricarbon monosulfide
label: mol:HC3S+
latex_body: The detection of \ce{HC3S+} was reported by \citet{Cernicharo:2021:L3b} in Yebes 40-m observations of TMC-1.  They identify and assign four lines in their spectra to the $J = 6\rightarrow5$, $J = 7\rightarrow6$, $J = 8\rightarrow7$, and $J = 9\rightarrow8$ transitions between 32.8--49.2\,GHz.  The initial assignment was based on quantum chemical calculations in the same paper, as well as from \citet{Thorwirth:2020:e1776409}.   Laboratory spectroscopy presented in the same paper confirms the detection.

name: thioketene
label: mol:H2CCS
note: Dipole is from Georgiou et al. 1979.
latex_body: \citet{Cernicharo:2021:L3} reported the detection of \ce{H2CCS} in Yebes 40-m observations of TMC-1.  They identify and assign the $3_{1,2} - 2_{1,1}$, $3_{1,3} - 2_{1,2}$, $4_{1,3} - 3_{1,2}$, $4_{1,4} - 3_{1,3}$, $3_{0,3} - 2_{0,2}$, and $4_{0,4} - 3_{0,3}$ transitions between 33.4--44.8\,GHz based on laboratory work by \citet{Georgiou:1979:365}, \citet{Winnewisser:1980:483}, and \citet{McNaughton:1996:377}.

name: tetracarbon monosulfide
label: mol:C4S
note: Dipole moment from Lee 1997 Chem Phys Lett 268, 69 and Pascoli & Lavendy 1998 Int J Mass Spectr 181, 11
latex_body: The detection of \ce{C4S} was reported by \citet{Cernicharo:2021:L3} in Yebes 40-m observations of TMC-1.  They identify and assign the $N_J = 10_{11} \rightarrow 9_{10}$, $N_J = 11_{12} \rightarrow 10_{11}$, $N_J = 12_{13} \rightarrow 11_{12}$, and $N_J = 13_{14} \rightarrow 12_{13}$ transitions between 32.6--41.5\,GHz based on the laboratory work of \citet{Hirahara:1993:L113} and \citet{Gordon:2001:311}.  The dipole moment was taken from the work of \citet{Lee:1997:69}.

name: monothioformic acid
label: mol:CHOSH
note: Dataset was refit by H.S.P. Müller for CDMS, and those are the predictions used for the detection.

name: tricarbon monoxide
label: mol:HC3O
note: Dipole from Cooksy et al. 1995 J Phys Chem 99, 11095

name: magnesium cyanoethynyl cation
label: mol:MgC3N+
note: Detection based on calculations

name: protonated acetylene
label: mol:C2H3+
note: Dipole from Lee & Shcaefer 1986 JCP 85, 3437

name: cyanoacetylene cation
label: mol:HC3N+
note: Identified from theory work provided in same paper

name: cyanoethynylsulfanyl
label: mol:NC3S
note: Detection based on a combination of calculations + the provided lab ref

name: methanol
label: mol:CH3OH
latex_body: \citet{Ball:1970:L203} reported the detection of \ce{CH3OH} in NRAO 140-ft observations of Sgr A and Sgr B2.  The $J_{K_a,K_c} = 1_{1,0}\rightarrow1_{1,1}$ transition at 834~MHz was observed and assigned based on laboratory work described in the same manuscript.

name: methyl cyanide
label: mol:CH3CN
latex_body: \ce{CH3CN} was detected by \citet{Solomon:1971:L107} in Sgr B2 and Sgr A using the NRAO 36-foot telescope.  Two fully resolved, and two blended $K$ components of the $J = 6\rightarrow5$ transition near 110.4~GHz were identified and assigned based on the laboratory data catalogued in \citet{Cord:1968:}.  It is likely that the frequencies listed in \citet{Cord:1968:} were obtained from, or relied heavily upon, the prior work by \citet{Kessler:1950:54}.  \ce{CH3CN} is also referred to as acetonitrile.

name: formamide
label: mol:NH2CHO
latex_body: The detection of \ce{NH2CHO} was reported by \citet{Rubin:1971:L39} in NRAO 140-ft observations of Sgr B2.  The $J_{K_a,K_c} = 2_{1,1}\rightarrow2_{1,2}$, $F = 2\rightarrow2$ and $1\rightarrow1$ hyperfine components were resolved, while the $3\rightarrow3$ was detected as part of a blend with the H112$\alpha$ transition.  The enabling laboratory spectroscopy was reported in the same manuscript. \ce{NH2CHO} was the first interstellar molecule detected containing H, C, N, and O.

name: methyl mercaptan
label: mol:CH3SH
latex_body: \citet{Linke:1979:L139} reported the detection of \ce{CH3SH} in Bell 7-m telescope observations of Sgr B2.  Six transitions between 76--102~GHz were identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Kilb:1955:1736} and unpublished data of D.R. Johnson.  This latter dataset was analyzed and formed the foundation of the more extensive work of \citet{Lees:1980:1640}.

name: ethylene
label: mol:C2H4
latex_body: The detection of \ce{C2H4} was reported by \citet{Betz:1981:L103} toward IRC+10216 using the 1.5-m McMath Solar Telescope.  Three rotationally-resolved ro-vibrational transitions were observed in the $\nu_7$ state: the $J_{K_a,K_c} = 5_{1,5}\rightarrow5_{0,5}$ at 28.5~THz was assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Lambeau:1980:227}, while the $1_{1,0}\rightarrow0_{0,0}$ and $8_{0,8}\rightarrow8_{1,8}$ were assigned based on laboratory work described in \citet{Betz:1981:L103}.

name: pentynylidyne radical
label: mol:C5H
note: *See also Cernicharo et al. 1986 A&A 167, L5 and Cernicharo et al. 1987 A&A 172, L5
latex_body: A tentative detection of \ce{C5H} was reported by \citet{Cernicharo:1986:L1} in IRAM 30-m observations of IRC+10216.  They identify a series of lines that could be assigned to a radical species in a $^2\Pi$ ground state with quantum numbers $J = 31/2\rightarrow29/2$ and $35/2\rightarrow33/2$ through $43/2\rightarrow41/2$ between 74--103~GHz.  Based on comparison of the derived rotational constant ($B_0 = 2387$~MHz) to a calculated rotational constant ($B_0 = 2375$~MHz) described in the same manuscript, they tentatively assigned the emission to the \ce{C5H} radical.  The subsequent laboratory work by \citet{Gottlieb:1986:L5} confirmed the assignment, and the interstellar identifications were extended shortly thereafter by \citet{Cernicharo:1986:L5} and \citet{Cernicharo:1987:L5}.

name: methyl isocyanide
label: mol:CH3NC
note: *Confirmed in Remijan et al. 2005 ApJ 632, 333 and Gratier et al. 2013 557, A101
latex_body: A tentative detection of \ce{CH3NC} was reported by \citet{Cernicharo:1988:L1} in IRAM 30-m observations of Sgr B2.  Somewhat blended signal was observed near the frequencies corresponding to the $J = 4\rightarrow3$, $5\rightarrow4$, and $7\rightarrow6$ transitions at 80.4, 100.5, and 140.7~GHz, respectively.  Although no reference is given for these frequencies, they were presumably enabled by the laboratory work of \citet{Kukolich:1972:869} and \citet{Ring:1947:1262}.  The detection was confirmed nearly two decades later in GBT 100-m observations of Sgr B2 by \citet{Remijan:2005:333} who observed the $J_K = 1_0\rightarrow0_0$ transition in absorption at 20.1~GHz and by \citet{Gratier:2013:A101} who observed three lines in the $J = 5\rightarrow4$ transition at 100.5~GHz with the IRAM 30-m toward the Horsehead PDR.

name: propynal
label: mol:HC2CHO
latex_body: \citet{Irvine:1988:L89} reported the detection of \ce{HC2CHO} in NRAO 140-ft and Nobeyama 45-m observations of TMC-1.  The $J_{K_a,K_c} = 2_{0,2}\rightarrow1_{0,1}$ and $4_{0,4}\rightarrow3_{0,3}$ transitions at 18.7 and 37.3~GHz, respectively, were assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Winnewisser:1973:16}.

name: butatrienylidene
label: mol:H2C4
latex_body: \citet{Cernicharo:1991:L43} reported the detection of the \ce{H2C4} carbene molecule in IRAM 30-m observations of IRC+10216.
