Eight transitions with $J$ values between 8--15 where identified and assigned between 80--135~GHz based on the laboratory spectroscopy of \citet{Killian:1990:L89}.

name: pentacarbon monosulfide radical
label: mol:C5S
note: *Confirmed in Agúndez et al. 2014 A&A 570, A45
latex_body: The \ce{C5S} radical was tentatively detected by \citet{Bell:1993:L37} in NRAO 140-ft telescope observations of IRC+10216.  A weak line corresponding to the $J = 13\rightarrow12$ transition of \ce{C5S} was identified near 23960~MHz based on the laboratory work of \citet{Kasai:1993:L45}.  The detection was confirmed in \citet{Agundez:2014:A45} with IRAM 30-m observations of IRC+10216.  The $J = 44\rightarrow43$, $45\rightarrow44$, and $46\rightarrow45$ transitions at 81.2, 83.0, and 84.9~GHz, respectively, were identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Gordon:2001:311}.

name: protonated cyanoacetylene
label: mol:HC3NH+
latex_body: \citet{Kawaguchi:1994:L95} reported the detection of \ce{HC3NH^+} in Nobeyama 45-m observations of TMC-1.  The $J = 4\rightarrow3$ and $5\rightarrow4$ transitions at 34.6 and 43.3~GHz, respectively, were identified and assigned based on the frequencies reported by \citet{Lee:1987:L145} from infrared difference frequency laser spectroscopy.  Using the astronomically detected pure rotational lines as a guide, the rotational spectrum was then measured in the laboratory by \citet{Gottlieb:2000:1910}.

name: cyanobutadiynyl radical
label: mol:C5N
latex_body: The \ce{C5N} radical was detected by \citet{Guelin:1998:L1} in Effelsberg 100-m and IRAM 30-m observations of TMC-1.  Two sets of hyperfine components of the $J = 17/2\rightarrow15/2$ and $65/2\rightarrow63/2$ transitions of \ce{C5N} at 25.2 and 89.8~GHz, respectively, were identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Kasai:1997:L65}.

name: diacetylene
label: mol:HC4H
note: *Confirmed in 2018 ApJ 852, 80
latex_body: \citet{Cernicharo:2001:L123} reported the detection of \ce{HC4H} in ISO observations of CRL 618 near 15.9~$\mu$m.  The observed absorption signal was identified and assigned to the $\nu_8$ fundamental bending mode of \ce{HC4H} based on the laboratory work of \citet{Arie:1992:195}.

name: cyanoethynylmethylene
label: mol:HC4N
latex_body: The \ce{HC4N} radical was detected by \citet{Cernicharo:2004:L145} in IRAM 30-m observations of IRC+10216.  A dozen transitions beteween 83--97~GHz were identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Tang:1999:69}.

name: cyclopropenone
label: mol:c-H2C3O
latex_body: \citet{Hollis:2006:933} reported the detection of \ce{c-H2C3O} in GBT 100-m observations of Sgr B2.  Six transitions between 9.3--44.6~GHz were identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Benson:1973:2772} and \citet{Guillemin:1990:190}.

name: ketenimine
label: mol:CH2CNH
latex_body: The detection of \ce{CH2CNH} was reported by \citet{Lovas:2006:L137} using GBT 100-m telescope observations of Sgr B2.  The $J_{K_a,K_c} = 9_{1,8}\rightarrow10_{0,10}$, $8_{1,7}\rightarrow9_{0,9}$, and $7_{1,6}\rightarrow8_{0,8}$ transitions at 4.9, 23.2, and 41.5~GHz, respectively, were identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Rodler:1984:447} and \citet{Rodler:1986:267}.

name: cyanobutadiynyl anion
label: mol:C5N-
latex_body: \citet{Cernicharo:2008:L83} reported the detection of \ce{C5N^-} in IRAM 30-m observations of IRC+10216.  They identify and assign 11 lines to the $J = 29\rightarrow28$ through $40\rightarrow39$ transitions of \ce{C5N^-} by comparison to the calculated rotational constants presented in \citet{Botschwina:2008:044305}.  To date, there does not appear to be a published pure rotational laboratory spectrum of this species.

name: E-cyanomethanimine
label: mol:HNCHCN
latex_body: \ce{HNCHCN} was detected in GBT 100-m telescope observations of Sgr B2 as reported by \citet{Zaleski:2013:L10}.  Nine transitions between 9.6--47.8~GHz were identified and assigned based on laboratory spectroscopy presented in the same manuscript.

name: silyl cyanide
label: mol:SiH3CN
note: *Confirmed in Cernicharo et al. 2017 A&A 606, L5
latex_body: The tentative detection of \ce{SiH3CN} was reported by \citet{Agundez:2014:A45} in IRAM 30-m observations of IRC+10216 through the identification of three weak emission features that they assign to the $J = 9\rightarrow8$, $10\rightarrow9$, and $11\rightarrow10$ transitions of \ce{SiH3CN} at 89.5, 99.5, and 109.4~GHz, respectively, based on the laboratory work of \citet{Priem:1998:183}.  The detection was confirmed by \citet{Cernicharo:2017:L5} through the detection of additional, higher-frequency transitions in this source.

name: magnesium butadiynyl radical
label: mol:MgC4H
note: Lab spectroscopy is electronic - no pure rotational spectra are available for this species.  Assignment was made based on quantum chemical calculations performed in Cernicharo et al. 2019.
latex_body: \citet{Cernicharo:2019:L2} reported the detection of \ce{MgC4H} in IRAM 30-m and Yebes 40-m observations of IRC+10216.  A series of doublet lines between {71.8--110.5}\,GHz were identified and assigned based on quantum chemical calculations and comparison to constants derived from electronic spectra reported by \citet{Forthomme:2010:116}.  To date, there has been no laboratory confirmation of these assignments by pure-rotational spectroscopy.

name: acetyl cation
label: mol:CH3CO+
latex_body: The detection of \ce{CH3CO+} was reported by \citet{Cernicharo:2021:L7} in IRAM 30-m and Yebes 40-m observations of TMC-1, {L483, L1527, and L1544}.  Four lines corresponding to the $J = 2\rightarrow1$, $J = 4\rightarrow3$, $J = 5\rightarrow4$, and $J = 6\rightarrow5$ transitions of \ce{CH3CO+} at 36.5, 73.1, 91.3, and 109.6\,GHz were identified and assigned based on laboratory spectroscopy presented in the same paper.

name: propadienthione
label: mol:H2CCCS
latex_body: \citet{Cernicharo:2021:L3} reported the detection of \ce{H2CCCS} in Yebes 40-m observations of TMC-1.  They identify and assign nine transitions between 35.3--45.5\,GHz based on the laboratory work from \citet{Brown:1988:789}.

note: Dipole moment taken from Kupper et al. 2002 JCP 117, 647

name: N-cyanomethanimine
label: mol:H2CNCN
note: Dipole from Bak et al. 1978 Chem Phys Lett 59, 330 and Back & Svanholt 1980 Chem Phys Lett 75, 528

name: acetaldehyde
label: mol:CH3CHO
note: Schutte et al. 1999 A&A 343, 966 reported a tentative detection in ices
latex_body: The detection of the $J_{K_a,K_c} = 1_{1,1}\rightarrow1_{1,0}$ transition of \ce{CH3CHO} at 1065~MHz was reported by \citet{Gottlieb:1973:181} in NRAO 140-ft observations of Sgr B2 and Sgr A.  The assignment was made based on the laboratory work of \citet{Kilb:1957:1695} and \citet{Souter:1970:674}.  \citet{Fourikis:1974:425} reported a confirming observation of the $2_{1,1}\rightarrow2_{1,2}$ transition in Parkes 64-m observations of Sgr B2 at 3195~MHz.

name: methylacetylene
label: mol:CH3CCH
latex_body: \citet{Buhl:1973:187} reported the detection of the $J_K = 5_0\rightarrow4_0$ transition of \ce{CH3CCH} at 85.4~GHz in NRAO 36-foot telescope observations of Sgr B2.  Although no reference to the source of the frequency is given, it was presumably obtained from the laboratory work of \citet{Trambarulo:1950:1613}.  Subsequent confirming transitions were observed at higher frequencies by \citet{Hollis:1981:541} and \citet{Kuiper:1984:211}.

name: methylamine
label: mol:CH3NH2
latex_body: The detection of \ce{CH3NH2} was simultaneously reported by \citet{Fourikis:1974:L139} and \citet{Kaifu:1974:L135}.  \citet{Kaifu:1974:L135} used the Mitaka 6-m and NRAO 36-ft telescopes to observe \ce{CH3NH2} toward Sgr B2 and Orion.  The $a$, $J_{K_a,K_c} = 5_{1,5}\rightarrow5_{0,5}$ and $s$, $4_{1,4}\rightarrow4_{0,4}$ transitions at 73 and 86~GHz, respectively, were assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Takagi:1973:L91}.  Using the same laboratory work, \citet{Fourikis:1974:L139} reported the detection of the $a$, $2_{0,2}\rightarrow1_{1,0}$ transition at 8.8~GHz using the Parkes 64-m telescope, also toward Sgr B2 and Orion.

name: vinyl cyanide
label: mol:CH2CHCN
latex_body: \ce{CH2CHCN}, also known as acrylonitrile, was detected by \citet{Gardner:1975:L127} in Parkes 64-m observations of Sgr B2.  The $J_{K_a,K_c} = 2_{1,1}\rightarrow2_{1,2}$ transition at 1372~MHz was identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Gerry:1973:1}.  Several additional confirming transitions were later observed in NRAO 140-ft telescope observations of TMC-1 by \citet{Matthews:1983:149}.

name: cyanodiacetylene
label: mol:HC5N
latex_body: \citet{Avery:1976:L173} reported the detection of \ce{HC5N} in Algonquin Radio Observatory 46-m telescope observations of Sgr B2.  They observed and assigned the $J = 4\rightarrow3$ transition at 10651~MHz based on the laboratory work of \citet{Alexander:1976:175}.  Later that year, \citet{Broten:1976:L143} observed the $1\rightarrow0$ and $8\rightarrow7$ transitions with the same facility, also in Sgr B2.

name: hexatriynyl radical
label: mol:C6H
latex_body: The first detection of the \ce{C6H} radical was made by \citet{Suzuki:1986:911} in Nobeyama 45-m observations of TMC-1.  The authors observed three sets of doublet transitions at 23.6, 40.2, and 43.0~GHz which they assigned to the hyperfine-split, $\Lambda$-doubled $J = 17/2\rightarrow15/2$, $29/2\rightarrow27/2$, and $31/2\rightarrow29/2$ transitions, respectively, of \ce{C6H} based on a comparison to the quantum chemical work of \citet{Murakami:1987:189}.  The detection was confirmed the following year with the measurement of the laboratory rotational spectrum by \citet{Pearson:1988:L13}.

name: ethylene oxide
label: mol:c-C2H4O
latex_body: \citet{Dickens:1997:753} reported the detection of \ce{c-C2H4O} in Nobeyama 45-m, Haystack 140-ft, and SEST 15-m telescope observations of Sgr B2.  Nine transitions between 39.6--254.2~GHz were identified and assigned based on the laboratory rotational spectroscopy performed by \citet{Hirose:1974:L145}.

events.summary: Detected in protoplanetary disks, C2H3DO detected in ISM

name: vinyl alcohol
label: mol:CH2CHOH
latex_body: \citet{Turner:2001:L207} reported the detection of both \emph{syn}- and \emph{anti}-vinyl alcohol in NRAO 12-m observation of Sgr B2.  The \emph{syn} conformer of \ce{CH2CHOH} is the more stable, but only two lines, the $J_{K_a,K_c} = 2_{1,2}\rightarrow1_{0,1}$ and $3_{1,3}\rightarrow2_{0,2}$ transitions at 86.6 and 103.7~GHz, respectively, were identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Kaushik:1977:89}.  In contrast, five transitions of the \emph{anti} conformer were identified between 71.8--154.5~GHz based on the laboratory work of \citet{Rodler:1985:23}.

name: hexatriynyl anion
label: mol:C6H-
note: *First gas-phase molecular anion
latex_body: The first molecular anion to be detected in the ISM, \citet{McCarthy:2006:L141} described both the observation and laboratory spectroscopic identification of \ce{C6H^-}.  More than a decade prior, \citet{Kawaguchi:1995:853} had noted the presence of a series of unidentified, harmonically spaced emission features in their Nobeyama 45-m survey of IRC+10216 dubbed B1377.  Based on their laboratory work, \citet{McCarthy:2006:L141} successfully assigned the carrier of these transitions to \ce{C6H^-}.  They also identified the $J = 4\rightarrow3$ and $5\rightarrow4$ transitions at 11.0 and 13.8~GHz, respectively, in GBT 100-m telescope observations of TMC-1.

name: methyl isocyanate
label: mol:CH3NCO
note: *see also Cernicharo et al. 2016 A&A 587, L4
latex_body: The detection of \ce{CH3NCO} was reported by \citet{Pilleri:2015:1} in ARO 12-m and SMT observations of Sgr B2.  They observed 17 uncontaminated emission lines of \ce{CH3NCO} between 68--116~GHz and assigned them based on laboratory work described in the same manuscript.  The following year, \citet{Cernicharo:2016:L4} reported the detection of the molecule in IRAM 30-m and ALMA data toward Orion, as well as extending the laboratory spectroscopy.

name: butadiynylformyl radical
label: mol:HC5O
latex_body: \citet{McGuire:2017:L28} reported the detection of \ce{HC5O} in GBT 100-m observations of TMC-1.  Four hyperfine-resolved components of the $J = 17/2\rightarrow15/2$ transition at 21.9~GHz were detected and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Mohamed:2005:234301}.

name: glycolonitrile
label: mol:HOCH2CN
latex_body: \citet{Zeng:2019:L43} reported the detection of \ce{HOCH2CN} in ALMA observations of IRAS 16293.  A total of 15 unblended transitions were identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of  \citet{Margules:2017:A50}.  \ce{HOCH2CN} is also known as hydroxyacetonitrile.

name: isocyanoacetylene
label: mol:HC4NC
note: Also known as isocyanobutadiyne
latex_body: The detection of \ce{HC4NC} in TMC-1 was nearly simultaneously reported by \cite{Xue:2020:L9} using GBT 100-m observations and \citet{Cernicharo:2020:L8} using Yebes 40-m observations.  \citet{Xue:2020:L9} reported the detection of the $J = 8\rightarrow7$, $J = 9\rightarrow8$, and $J = 10\rightarrow9$ transitions, as well as an overall detection significance of 10.5$\sigma$ based on spectral stacking and matched filtering analyses.  \citet{Cernicharo:2020:L8} reported the detection of the higher-lying $J = 12\rightarrow11$, $J = 13\rightarrow12$, $J = 14\rightarrow13$, $J = 15\rightarrow14$, and $J = 16\rightarrow15$ transitions.  Both studies relied on the laboratory work of \citet{Botschwina:1998:3108}.

name: propargylimine
label: mol:HC3HNH
latex_body: \citet{Bizzocchi:2020:A98} reported the detection of \ce{HC3HNH} in IRAM 30-m observations of G+0.639-0.027.  A total of 18 transitions of the Z-conformer were identified and assigned in the observational data between 73 -- 111\,GHz based on laboratory work described in the same paper as well as that of \citet{Kroto:1984:993}, \citet{Sugie:1985:83}, and \citet{McNaughton:1988:195}.

name: methyl formate
label: mol:HCOOCH3
note: The trans conformer was detected in Neill et al. 2012 ApJ 755, 143
latex_body: \citet{Brown:1975:L29} reported the detection of \emph{cis}-\ce{HCOOCH3} in Parkes 64-m telescope observations of Sgr B2.  Based on laboratory work presented in the same paper, they identified and assigned the $A$-state $J_{K_a,K_c} = 1_{1,0}\rightarrow1_{1,1}$ transition of \emph{cis}-\ce{HCOOCH3} at 1610.25~MHz.  Several months later, \citet{Churchwell:1975:229} confirmed the detection of the $A$-state line and additionally observed the $E$-state line of the same transition at 1610.9~MHz using the Effelsberg 100-m telescope.  Nearly three decades later, \citet{Neill:2012:153} reported the tentative identification of the higher-energy \emph{trans} conformer of \ce{HCOOCH3} in GBT 100-m telescope observations of Sgr B2, based on laboratory spectroscopy presented in the same work.  A total of seven transitions between 9.1--27.4~GHz were observed.

name: methylcyanoacetylene
label: mol:CH3C3N
latex_body: The detection of \ce{CH3C3N} was reported by \citet{Broten:1984:L25} in NRAO 140-ft observations of TMC-1.  A total of seven components of the $J = 5\rightarrow4$ through $8\rightarrow7$ transitions of \ce{CH3C3N} between 20.7--33.1~GHz were resolved and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Moises:1982:497}.

name: heptatriynylidyne radical
label: mol:C7H
latex_body: \citet{Guelin:1997:L1} reported the detection of the \ce{C7H} radical in IRAM 30-m telescope observations of IRC+10216.  Based on the laboratory spectroscopy of \citet{Travers:1996:L77}, they identified and assigned five rotational transitions between 83--86.6~GHz.

name: acetic acid
label: mol:CH3COOH
latex_body: The detection of \ce{CH3COOH} was reported by \citet{Mehringer:1997:L71} in BIMA and OVRO observations of Sgr B2.  The $J_{K_a,K_c} = 8_{*,8}\rightarrow7_{*,7}$ $A$ and $E$-state lines of \ce{CH3COOH} around 90.2~GHz, and the $9_{*,9}\rightarrow8_{*,8}$ $E$-state line at 100.9~GHz were identified and assigned based on the work of \citet{Tabor:1957:974} and \citet{Wlodarczak:1988:313}.

name: hexapentaenylidene
label: mol:H2C6
latex_body: \citet{Langer:1997:L63} reported the detection of \ce{H2C6} in Goldstone 70-m telescope observations of TMC-1.  The $J_{K_a,K_c} = 7_{1,7}\rightarrow6_{1,6}$ and $8_{1,8}\rightarrow7_{1,7}$ transitions of \ce{H2C6} at 18.8 and 21.5~GHz, respectively, were identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{McCarthy:1997:518}.

name: glycolaldehyde
label: mol:CH2OHCHO
latex_body: The detection of \ce{CH2OCHO} was reported by \citet{Hollis:2000:L107} in NRAO 12-m observations of Sgr B2.  A total of five transitions between 71.5--103.7~GHz were identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Marstokk:1973:259}.  Despite numerous claims in the astronomical literature, glycolaldehyde is not a true sugar, and is instead a diose, a 2-carbon monosaccharide, making it the simplest sugar-related molecule.

name: triacetylene
label: mol:HC6H
latex_body: \citet{Cernicharo:2001:L123} reported the detection of \ce{HC6H} in ISO observations of CRL 618.  The $\nu_{11}$ fundamental bending mode of \ce{HC6H} at 16.1~$\mu$m was observed and assigned based ont he laboratory work of \citet{Haas:1994:176}.

name: propenal
label: mol:CH2CHCHO
latex_body: A tentative detection of \ce{CH2CHCHO} was reported by \citet{Dickens:2001:643} in NRAO 12-m and SEST 15-m observations of G327.3-0.6 and Sgr B2.  They tentatively assigned six emission lines between 88.5--107.5~GHz to \ce{CH2CHCHO}, based on the laboratory work of \citet{Winnewisser:1975:1001}.  The detection was confirmed by \citet{Hollis:2004:L21} in GBT 100-m telescope observations of Sgr B2.  They observed and assigned the $J_{K_a,K_c} = 2_{1,1}\rightarrow1_{1,0}$ and $3_{1,3}\rightarrow2_{1,2}$ transitions at 18.2 and 26.1~GHz, respectively, based on the laboratory work of \citet{Blom:1984:7427}.  \ce{CH2CHCHO} is also referred to as acrolein.

name: cyanoallene
label: mol:CH2CCHCN

latex_body: The detection of \emph{trans}-\ce{CH3CH2OH} was reported by \citet{Zuckerman:1975:L99} in NRAO 36-foot telescope observations of Sgr B2.  The $J_{K_a,K_c} = 6_{0,6}\rightarrow5_{1,5}$, $4_{1,4}\rightarrow3_{0,3}$, and $5_{1,5}\rightarrow4_{0,4}$ transitions at 85.3, 90.1, and 104.8~GHz, respectively, were identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Takano:1968:157}.  The \emph{gauche} substates of \ce{CH3CH2OH} were later identified as the carriers of 14 previously unidentified emission features in the Nobeyama 45-m observations of Orion presented in \citet{Ohishi:1988:511} based on the laboratory work of \citet{Pearson:1997:420}.

Two dozen emission features between 88--116~GHz were identified and assigned to \ce{CH3CH2CN} in Orion.  The foundational laboratory spectroscopy was reported by \citet{Heise:1974:1345}, \citet{Mader:1974:164}, and \citet{Laurie:1959:1500}.  Based on this work, additional higher-frequency lines were measured and assigned in \citet{Johnson:1977:370}.

name: cyanotriacetylene
label: mol:HC7N
latex_body:
Reports of the detection of \ce{HC7N} were made nearly simultaneously by \citet{Little:1978:45P} (4 January) and \citet{Kroto:1978:L133} (1 February), although the former acknowledges an earlier report by \citet{Kroto:1977:303} (13 June).  A few months later (5 October), \citet{Winnewisser:1978:L37} also reported the detection of \ce{HC7N}. 
	
	The observations of \citet{Kroto:1977:303} and \citet{Kroto:1978:L133} were conducted toward TMC-1 using both the Algonquin 46-m and Haystack 36.6-m telescopes.  \citet{Kroto:1977:303} reported the observation of the $J = 9\rightarrow8$ transition at 10.2~GHz, while \citet{Kroto:1978:L133} additionally observed the $21\rightarrow20$ transition at 23.7~GHz.  The assignments were based on laboratory work carried out by a subset of the authors of \citet{Kroto:1978:L133}, which they would later report in \citet{Kirby:1980:261}.
	
	\citet{Little:1978:45P} used the SRC Appleton Laboratory 25-m telescope to observe the $22\rightarrow21$ transition at 24.8~GHz in both TMC-1 and TMC-2.  The rotational constants required for the detection were provided by H. W. Kroto.
	
	The work of \citet{Winnewisser:1978:L37} was presumably carried out independently, as there were no references to the previous three manuscripts in this paper. They reported the detection of the $21\rightarrow20$ transition in IRC+10216.  Although the facility used for the observations is not named in the main portion of the manuscript, the authors acknowledge the operators of Effelsberg, and cite a beam size of 40$^{\prime\prime}$ near 24~GHz, which is reasonably close to that of a 100-m telescope.  There is also no reference given to the source of the rotational transition frequency, nor is a frequency actually given.

name: methyldiacetylene
label: mol:CH3C4H
latex_body:
The detection of \ce{CH3C4H} was nearly simultaneously reported by \citet{Walmsley:1984:L11} (22 March) and \citet{MacLeod:1984:L89} (15 July).  Later that year, \citet{Loren:1984:L23} (1 November) also reported an independent detection, having received word of the earlier work during the publication process.
	
	\citet{Walmsley:1984:L11} reported the detection in observations of TMC-1 using the Effelsberg 100-m telescope. They observed and assigned the $K = 0$ and $K = 1$ components of the $J = 6\rightarrow5$ and $5\rightarrow4$ transitions at 24.4 and 20.3~GHz, respectively.  Their assignments were based on the laboratory work of \citet{Heath:1955:38}, although they suggest the astronomical observations might be used to refine those measurements moving forward.
	
	Both \citet{MacLeod:1984:L89} and \citet{Loren:1984:L23} observed the same transitions in TMC-1, the former using the Haystack 36.6-m and NRAO 140-foot telescopes, while the latter used solely the NRAO 140-foot.

name: octatriynyl radical
label: mol:C8H
latex_body: \citet{Cernicharo:1996:L27} reported the detection of the \ce{C8H} radical in IRAM 30-m observations of IRC+10216, as well as in the archival Nobeyama 45-m observations of \citet{Kawaguchi:1995:853}.  They identified and assigned ten transitions between 31.1--83.9~GHz based on comparison to calculated rotational constants from \citet{Pauzat:1991:L13}.  The detection and assignment was confirmed in an accompanying letter by the laboratory work of \citet{McCarthy:1996:L31}.

name: acetamide
label: mol:CH3CONH2
latex_body: The detection of \ce{CH3CONH2} was reported toward Sgr B2 by \citet{Hollis:2006:L25} using the GBT 100-m telescope.  A total of eight transitions between 9.3--47.4~GHz were identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Suenram:2001:188} and \citet{Ilyushin:2004:115}.

name: octatriynyl anion
label: mol:C8H-
latex_body: \citet{Brunken:2007:L43} and \citet{Remijan:2007:L47} simultaneously reported the detection of \ce{C8H^-}.  Both detections were made with the GBT 100-m telescope; the former described the detection in TMC-1 while the latter was toward IRC+10216.  \citet{Remijan:2007:L47} detected the $J = 22\rightarrow21$ and $35\rightarrow34$ through $38\rightarrow37$ transitions between 25.7--44.3~GHz based on the laboratory work of \citet{Gupta:2007:L57}.  \citet{Brunken:2007:L43} observed the $11\rightarrow10$ through $13\rightarrow12$, and the $16\rightarrow15$ transitions between 12.8--18.7~GHz, based on the same laboratory work.

label: mol:CH2CHCH3
latex_body: The detection of \ce{CH2CHCH3}, also referred to as propene, was reported by \citet{Marcelino:2007:L127} in IRAM 30-m observations of TMC-1.  A total of thirteen rotational transitions between 84.2--103.7~GHz were identified and assigned based on the laboratory work of \citet{Wlodarczak:1994:239} and \citet{Pearson:1994:120}.

latex_body: \citet{Kolesnikova:2014:L7} reported the detection of \ce{CH3CH2SH} in IRAM 30-m observations of Orion.  A total of 77 unblended lines between 80--280~GHz were identified and assigned based on laboratory spectroscopy presented in the same manuscript.  Subsequent attempts to identify the molecule in Sgr B2(N) by \citet{Muller:2016:A92} were unsuccessful.  \citet{Rodriguez-Almeida:2021:L11} confirm the presence of \ce{CH3CH2SH} in the ISM using IRAM 30-m and Yebes 40-m observations of G+0.693-0.027 based on the laboratory work of \citet{Schmidt:1975:3864}, \citet{Kolesnikova:2014:L7} and \citet{Muller:2016:A92}.

name: hexadiynylformyl radical
label: mol:HC7O
note: *Confirmed in Cordiner et al. 2017 ApJ 850, 194
latex_body: \citet{McGuire:2017:L28} reported the tentative detection of the \ce{HC7O} radical in GBT 100-m observations of TMC-1.  Based on the laboratory work of \citet{Mohamed:2005:234301}, a weak detection of the $J = 35/2\rightarrow33/2$ transition with partially resolved hyperfine structure was observed near 19.2~GHz.  The detection was confirmed in \citet{Cordiner:2017:187} by the observation of several additional weak features, without hyperfine structure, corresponding to the $33/2\rightarrow31/2$ transitions near 18.1~GHz.  A composite average of these lines, plus the data from \citet{McGuire:2017:L28}, provided a 9.5$\sigma$ detection.

latex_body: \citet{Lee:2021:L11} reported the detection of the $trans$-(E) conformer of \ce{HCCCHCHCN} in GBT 100-m observations of TMC-1.  They identify and assign the $8_{0,8} - 7_{0,7}$, $9_{0,9} - 8_{0,8}$, and $9_{1,9} - 8_{1,8}$ transitions at 23.2, 26.1, and 25.9\,GHz based on the laboratory work of \citet{Halter:2001:12353}, \citet{Thorwirth:2004:93}, and \citet{McCarthy:2020:5170}.  Using spectral line stacking and matched filtering techniques, a significance of 8.0$\sigma$ was placed on the detection.  Using these same techniques, tentative signal from the $trans$-(Z) conformer was identified at 2.8$\sigma$ significance.

name: ethyl methyl ether
label: mol:C2H5OCH3
note: A tentative detection was claimed in 2005 (Fuchs et al. 2005 A&A 444, 521) and disputed in Carroll et al. 2015 ApJ 799, 15.  Although they do not claim it in the paper as confirmation or a first detection, convincing lines are shown in Tercero et al. 2018 A&A 620, L6.
latex_body: \citet{Charnley:2001:685} indicated a tentative detection of \ce{C2H5OCH3} in NRAO 12-m and BIMA observations of Orion-KL and Sgr B2(N).  A detection of \ce{C2H5OCH3} was then later reported by \citet{Fuchs:2005:521} in IRAM 30-m and SEST 15-m observations of W51e2.  This detection was disputed by \citet{Carroll:2015:15}, who re-observed both W51e2 and Sgr B2(N) using the ARO 12-m and GBT 100-m telescopes, and failed to detect \ce{C2H5OCH3}, setting an upper limit column density substantially lower than the reported value of \citet{Fuchs:2005:521}.  Evidence supporting the tentative detection in Orion-KL was later reported by \citet{Tercero:2015:L1} using IRAM 30-m and ALMA observations of the region, although the authors claim the detection should still be viewed as tentative.  The laboratory spectroscopy was performed by \citet{Hayashi:1975:147} and \citet{Fuchs:2003:277}.

A 5.8$\sigma$ detection was reported based on spectral line stacking and matched filtering using laboratory work reported in the same paper as well as that of \citet{Ford:1978:326} and \citet{Sakaizumi:1987:3903}.  \citet{Lee:2021:L2a} subsequently published the detections of the $7_{2,5} - 6_{2,4}$, $7_{1,6} - 6_{1,5}$, $8_{0,8} - 7_{0,7}$, and $9_{0,9} - 8_{0,8}$ transitions in the same source, citing an increased detection significance of 10.7$\sigma$.  1-\ce{C5H5CN} is the first molecule to be reported in the ISM containing a five-membered ring.

label: mol:2-C10H7CN

latex_body: \citet{McGuire:2021:1265a} reported the detection of 2-cyanonaphthalene in GBT 100-m observations of TMC-1.  A 17.1$\sigma$ detection was claimed based on a spectral matched filtering analysis, using the laboratory work of \citet{McNaughton:2018:5268a}.  No individual rotational transitions were observed at $\geq$3$\sigma$.

name: buckminsterfullerene
label: mol:C60
note: *See also Sellgren et al. 2010 ApJ 722, L54 and Werner 2004b, Sellgren 2007 therein
latex_body: \citet{Cami:2010:1180} reported the detection of \ce{C60} in \emph{Spitzer} observations of Tc~1.  Strong emission features from \ce{C60} at 7.0, 85, 17.4, and 18.9~$\mu$m were identified and assigned based on the work of \citet{Martin:1993:14607} and \citet{Fabian:1996:13864}.

name: buckminsterfullerene cation
label: mol:C60+
note: *See also Campbell et al. 2015 Nature 523, 322
latex_body: \citet{Berne:2013:L4} reported the detection of \ce{C60^+} in \emph{Spitzer} observations toward NGC 7023.  Two emission features at 7.1 and 6.4~$\mu$m were assigned to \ce{C60^+} based on the laboratory matrix-isolation work of \citet{Kern:2013:8251}.  A number of additional features were assigned based on theoretical calculations performed and described in \citet{Berne:2013:L4}.  Subsequent laboratory work by \citet{Campbell:2015:322a} confirmed the presence of \ce{C60^+} in the ISM by measuring the gas-phase spectrum of \ce{C60^+}.  Based on those results, they determined that \ce{C60^+} was the carrier of the 9632 and 9577~\AA~diffuse interstellar bands, the first definitive molecular assignment of a carrier of one of these bands.  Follow-up observational and laboratory studies by \citet{Pilleri:2015:1} and \citet{Campbell:2016:17} solidified the identification.

name: rugbyballene
label: mol:C70
latex_body:
\citet{Cami:2010:1180} reported the detection of \ce{C70} in \emph{Spitzer} observations of Tc~1. They identified and assigned four emission features between 12--22~$\mu$m to \ce{C70} based on the work of \citet{Nemes:1994:295}, \citet{vonCzarnowski:1995:321}, and \citet{Stratmann:1998:483}.

name: aziridine
label: mol:c-C2H4NH
latex_body: \citet{Dickens:2001:643} reported the tentative detection of the $J_{K_a,K_c} = 5_{5,0}\rightarrow4_{4,1}$ transition of \ce{c-C2H4NH}, also known as ethylenimine, at 226~GHz toward Sgr B2, G34.3+0.2, G10.47+0.03, and G327.3-0.6 in observations made with the SEST 15-m, NRAO 12-m, and NASA Deep Space Network 70-m telescopes.  The laboratory data were reported by \citet{Thorwirth:2000:323,Thorwirth:2000:116,Tolles:1965:2253}.

name: acetylide anion
label: mol:C2H-
latex_body: \citet{Cernicharo:2008:L83} suggest that an unidentified line at 83.278\,GHz, classified as U83278, in IRAM 30-m observations of IRC+10216 may be due to the $J = 1\rightarrow0$ transition of \ce{C2H-}.  Although they list no source for their line frequency, it presumably is derived from the work of \citet{Brunken:2007:L33} and \citet{Amano:2008:244305}.

name: iron monoxide
label: mol:FeO
latex_body: \citet{Walmsley:2002:L109} identified an absorption feature in IRAM 30-m observations of Sgr B2 at 153~GHz that they tentatively assign to the $J = 5\rightarrow4$, $\Omega = 4$ transition of FeO, based on the laboratory work of \citet{Allen:1996:130}.  Later, \citet{Furuya:2003:L21} used the Nobeyama Millimeter Array to confirm the detection of this line, but no additional transitions were observed.  Most recently, \citet{Decin:2018:113} reported a tentative detection of the $11\rightarrow10$, $\Omega = 4$ transition in ALMA observations of R Dor at 337~GHz.

name: glycine
label: mol:NH2CH2COOH
latex_body: \citet{Kuan:2003:848} reported a detection of 27 lines of \ce{NH2CH2COOH} in observations toward Orion, Sgr B2, and W51 using the NRAO 12-m telescope.  Each source contained 13--16 of the 27 features; three features were seen in common between the sources.  The frequencies were obtained from the rotational constants measured and reported in \citet{Suenram:1980:7180} and \citet{Lovas:1995:L201}.  The detection was later disputed by \citet{Snyder:2005:914}, who claimed to have identified a number of issues with the analysis.  Notably, \citet{Snyder:2005:914} argue that the frequency predictions used by \citet{Kuan:2003:848} were extrapolated too far above the measured laboratory transitions.  \citet{Snyder:2005:914} used laboratory frequencies from \citet{Ilyushin:2005:15} that covered the observed frequency range, and examined archival NRAO 12-m and SEST 15-m observations of Orion, Sgr B2, and W51.  They report a number of ``missing'' transitions of \ce{NH2CH2COOH} that they predicted should have been strongly detected, if the detection of \citet{Kuan:2003:848} held.  Subsequent searches by \citet{Jones:2007:579}, \citet{Cunningham:2007:1201}, and \citet{Belloche:2008:179} using both interferometers and single-dish facilities failed to detect \ce{NH2CH2COOH}, and set upper limits to the column density lower than that claimed in the detection of \citet{Kuan:2003:848} (see \citealt{Belloche:2008:179} \S4.4 for a detailed discussion).

name: protonated cyanodiacetylene cation
label: mol:HC5NH+
latex_body: \citet{Marcelino:2020:L6} report a tentative detection of \ce{HC5NH+} in Yebes 40-m observations of TMC-1.  They identify a series of eight harmonically spaced lines in the data corresponding to a rotational constant $B$ = 1295.8158\,MHz.  Based on quantum chemical calculations, they suggest either \ce{HC5NH+} or \ce{NC4NH+} as the potential carrier, eventually proposing \ce{HC5NH+} as the more likely.

name: cyanophosphaethyne
label: mol:NCCP
latex_body: \citet{Agundez:2014:A45} reported the tentative detection of \ce{NCCP} in IRAM 30-m observations of IRC+10216.  They identified and tentatively assigned three signals in their spectra to the $J = 15\rightarrow14$, $16\rightarrow15$, and $18\rightarrow17$ transitions of \ce{NCCP} at 81, 87, and 97~GHz, respectively, based on the laboratory work of \citet{Bizzocchi:2001:110}.

name: nitric oxide cation
label: mol:NO+
latex_body: \citet{Cernicharo:2014:40} reported the tentative detection of a single line ($J = 2\rightarrow1$) of \ce{NO+} at 238~GHz toward B1-b using the IRAM 30-m telescope.  The assignment was made based on laboratory rotational spectroscopy described in the same paper.

name: cyanate anion
label: mol:OCN-
latex_body: There is a long history of attempts to identify the carrier of the ``XCN" feature in astrophyiscal ice observations near 2167~cm$^{-1}$.  On the basis of extensive laboratory work (see, e.g., \citealt{Schutte:1997:L43}), \citet{vanBroekhuizen:2005:249} claim an identification of \ce{OCN-} in ices along numerous sightlines to low-mass YSO's using the Very Large Telescope (VLT).  Only a single absorption feature could be ascribed to \ce{OCN-}.  As this is a single feature detection, and no gas-phase detection has been claimed, \ce{OCN-} has been listed as a tentative interstellar species in this census.

name: phenol
label: mol:c-C6H5OH
latex_body: \citet{Kolesnikova:2013:13} reported the laboratory rotational spectroscopy of \ce{C6H5OH}, and identified a number of coincidences between transitions of \ce{C6H5OH} and unassigned lines in IRAM 30-m observations of Orion between 80--280~GHz from \citep{Tercero:2012:A119}.

name: silylidyne
label: mol:SiH
latex_body: \citet{Schilke:2001:281} reported the tentative detection of two features in a CSO line survey of Orion that were coincident with transitions of SiH.  Two groups of hyperfine transitions in the $^2\Pi _{1/2}$ state at 625 and 628~GHz fell within range of the observations.  The lower set is significantly blended with other emitting species, whereas the higher-frequency set appears unblended, and may show partially resolved hyperfine structure.  The laboratory frequencies were from \citet{Brown:1985:188}.

name: 1-cyano propargyl radical
label: mol:HCCCHCN
latex_body: \citet{Cabezas:2025:L14} reported the detection of HCCCHCN in Yebes 40m observations of TMC-1.  They identify and assign seven rotational transitions, some with resolved hyperfine components, between 31--44 GHz based on laboratory data presented in \citet{Cabezas:2022:A24}.

name: thioacetaldehyde
label: mol:CH3CHS
latex_body: The detection of \ce{CH3CHS} was reported toward TMC-1 by \citet{Agundez:2025:L20} in Yebes 40m observations.  They detect seven total transitions, including resolved A/E splitting from the methyl internal rotor, based on laboratory work by \citet{Margules:2020:111304}, \citet{Kroto:1976:346}, and \citet{Kroto:1974:265}.

name: dimethyl sulfide
label: mol:CH3SCH3
latex_body: \citet{Sanz-Novo:2025:L37} reported the detection of \ce{CH3SCH3} in Yebes 40 m and IRAM 30m observations toward G+0.693-0.027.  They report the detection of 10 clean transitions between 42 and 171 GHz based on spectroscopic data presented in \citet{Ilyushin:2020:127114} which builds on an extensive history of laboratory investigations (e.g., \citealt{Rudolph:1960:742, Dreizler:1962:712, Demaison:1980:391, Jabri:2016:A127, Niide:2004:152, Pierce:1961:479}).

name: cyanocoronene
label: mol:C24H11CN
latex_body: \citet{Wenzel:2025:L36} reported the detection of cyanocoronene in GBT observations of TMC-1.  Ten individual transitions are identified at $\geq$3$\sigma$, and a spectral stacking and matched filter analysis \citep{Loomis:2021:188a} yielded an overall detection significance of 17.3$\sigma$.  The identification was based on laboratory measurements presented in the same work.
